literature.headline_zh: 禽流感病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期禽流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在野生鸟类中,共报告了17,091例高致病性禽流感H5检测,涉及1,467个县级地点。 [10.1371/journal.pone.0345354]
该更正确认了Kwang-Nyeong Lee 应被列为原始文章的共同通讯作者。在更正中未呈现新的结果。 [10.1007/s00705-026-06740-z]
DDX10特异性增强了人类适应型H1N1病毒(包括2009年大流行株)的聚合酶活性和复制,但对禽源H9N2病毒则无此作用。这种差异性活性与DDX10与人类来源PB1(Cal04/H1N1)相比,与禽源PB1(BJ16/H9N2)显示出更强的相互作用有关。 [10.1128/jvi.00815-26]
在致命挑战研究中,与单独接种A(H5)疫苗接种相比,季节性疫苗在A(H5)疫苗接种接种前的接种与一项小鼠实验中改善的结局相关,但在另外两项小鼠实验或雪貂中未观察到这种效果。 [10.1080/22221751.2026.2731495]
ARCT-2304耐受性良好,主要表现为轻度至中度、短暂且剂量依赖的招募不良事件,未发现安全性问题。两剂诱导了强效的HA和NA体液免疫应答。8周的给药间隔比4周的计划产生了更高的免疫应答幅度和更持久的免疫效果,第二剂后6至7个月,中和抗体和抗NA抗体仍显著升高。 [10.1038/s41467-026-78031-9]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。

literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: A total of 17,091 HPAI H5 detections were reported in wild birds across 1,467 county-level locations. [10.1371/journal.pone.0345354]

The correction identified that Kwang-Nyeong Lee should have been denoted as a co-corresponding author in the original article. No new results were presented in the correction. [10.1007/s00705-026-06740-z]
DDX10 selectively enhanced the polymerase activity and replication of human-adapted H1N1 viruses, including the 2009 pandemic strain, but not avian-origin H9N2 viruses. [10.1128/jvi.00815-26]

In lethal challenge studies, seasonal vaccine priming before A(H5) vaccination was associated with improved outcomes compared with A(H5) vaccination alone in one of three mouse experiments, but this effect was not observed in the other two mouse experiments or in ferrets. [10.1080/22221751.2026.2731495]

ARCT-2304 was well-tolerated, displaying mostly mild-to-moderate, transient, dose-dependent solicited AEs, with no safety concerns identified. Two doses elicited robust HA and NA humoral responses. [10.1038/s41467-026-78031-9]

news.headline_zh: 禽流感病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期禽流感病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 明尼苏达州H5N1禽流感活动正在增加,一项研究指出该病毒存在于北极熊中。 [news-bc0bfdec599d76ff]
一项研究分析了H5N1病毒B3.13基因型,发现其在奶牛中出现了值得关注的适应性变化,增强了在牛和人细胞中的复制能力。研究结果表明,该病毒正在积极适应哺乳动物,增加了向人类传播的潜在风险。 [news-3118988287a5978e]
FFAR和Entomol Products,LLC正在测试一种使用氢化猫薄荷油(HCO)的雾化方法,以减少 poultry housing 中的 禽流感 传播。 [news-24c14de57c9a1a31]
文章报道美国农业部动物检疫局在过去30天内记录了八例新的H5N1禽流感暴发,其中六例发生在明尼苏达州。一项新研究指出阿拉斯加北极熊中出现了H5N1禽流感。这些暴发包括商业和家禽 flock,以及 野生鸟类。 [news-6aeb4896df789e17]
根据质量保证与食品安全的报道,德克萨斯A&M农业生命部正在测试远紫外线光以防止禽流感在禽类中的传播。 [news-aa9aa8610fe66b21]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.headline_en: Recent Avian influenza A viruses news
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Avian influenza A viruses news developments.
key_findings_en: H5N1 avian flu activity is increasing in Minnesota, with a study noting the virus in polar bears. [news-bc0bfdec599d76ff]

A study examining the B3.13 genotype of H5N1 found concerning adaptations in cattle, enhancing replication in bovine and human cells. The findings suggest the virus is actively adapting to mammals, increasing the risk of zoonotic spillover. [news-3118988287a5978e]
FFAR and Entomol Products, LLC are testing a fogging approach using hydrogenated catmint oil (HCO) to reduce avian influenza transmission in poultry housing. [news-24c14de57c9a1a31]

The article reports that the USDA APHIS recorded eight new H5N1 avian flu outbreaks in the past 30 days, with six in Minnesota. A new study notes H5N1 avian flu in polar bears in Alaska. The outbreaks include both commercial and backyard flocks, as well as wild birds. [news-6aeb4896df789e17]
Texas A&M AgriLife is testing far-ultraviolet light to prevent bird flu in poultry, as reported by Quality Assurance & Food Safety. [news-aa9aa8610fe66b21]

papers.title: Spatiotemporal clustering of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 at the wild waterfowl-poultry interface: Vector-specific spillover risks in the U.S., 2022–2025
papers.abstract: The emergence of the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b in North America, beginning in February 2022, has highlighted the dynamic, unpredictable, and regionally variable risk of infections. Studies are needed to assess the spatiotemporal clustering of HPAI H5 at the interface between wild waterfowl and commercial poultry to better understand and mitigate this risk. Publicly available data on HPAI H5 detections in wild birds and commercial poultry from January 2022 to January 2026 were analyzed at the county level. Retrospective space-time permutation models were used to identify and scan for clusters with higher-than-expected detection rates. A total of 17,091 HPAI H5 detections were reported in wild birds across 1,467 county-level locations. Four species, Mallard ( Anas platyrhynchos ) (2,848 detections, 16.66%), Canada goose ( Branta canadensis ) (1,496, 8.75%), Green-winged teal ( Anas carolinensis ) (1,364, 7.98%), and Snow goose ( Anser caerulescens ) (1,084, 6.34%), accounted for 39.73% of detections. In commercial poultry, 532 outbreaks in turkey operations, 148 outbreaks in table-egg layer operations, 99 outbreaks in broiler chicken operations, and 89 outbreaks in commercial duck operations were reported, respectively. Several spillover events followed an east-to-west expansion. In early 2022, mallard detections preceded outbreaks in Northeast egg-layer and duck farms, while snow goose detections in the Upper Midwest coincided with turkey farm outbreaks. In the Pacific and Mountain West during summer 2022, detections in Canada geese overlapped with turkey farm outbreaks. A resurgence occurred in the Midwest (2025), with snow and Canada goose detections overlapping severe outbreaks in turkey and layer flocks. Additionally, in the Upper Midwest, Canada goose and mallard detections overlapped with outbreaks in commercial duck farms during fall-winter 2025. The study findings demonstrate distinct vector-based transmission dynamics of HPAI H5 at the wild waterfowl-poultry interface. Farm biosecurity strategies must adapt to these recurrent, vector-specific risks.

papers.title_zh: 在野生水禽-家禽界面上高致病性禽流感(高致病性禽流感)H5N1的时空聚集:美国媒介特定的跨物种溢出风险,2022–2025年
papers.source_body_en: The emergence of the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b in North America, beginning in February 2022, has highlighted the dynamic, unpredictable, and regionally variable risk of infections. Studies are needed to assess the spatiotemporal clustering of HPAI H5 at the interface between wild waterfowl and commercial poultry to better understand and mitigate this risk. Publicly available data on HPAI H5 detections in wild birds and commercial poultry from January 2022 to January 2026 were analyzed at the county level. Retrospective space-time permutation models were used to identify and scan for clusters with higher-than-expected detection rates. A total of 17,091 HPAI H5 detections were reported in wild birds across 1,467 county-level locations. Four species, Mallard ( Anas platyrhynchos ) (2,848 detections, 16.66%), Canada goose ( Branta canadensis ) (1,496, 8.75%), Green-winged teal ( Anas carolinensis ) (1,364, 7.98%), and Snow goose ( Anser caerulescens ) (1,084, 6.34%), accounted for 39.73% of detections. In commercial poultry, 532 outbreaks in turkey operations, 148 outbreaks in table-egg layer operations, 99 outbreaks in broiler chicken operations, and 89 outbreaks in commercial duck operations were reported, respectively. Several spillover events followed an east-to-west expansion. In early 2022, mallard detections preceded outbreaks in Northeast egg-layer and duck farms, while snow goose detections in the Upper Midwest coincided with turkey farm outbreaks. In the Pacific and Mountain West during summer 2022, detections in Canada geese overlapped with turkey farm outbreaks. A resurgence occurred in the Midwest (2025), with snow and Canada goose detections overlapping severe outbreaks in turkey and layer flocks. Additionally, in the Upper Midwest, Canada goose and mallard detections overlapped with outbreaks in commercial duck farms during fall-winter 2025. The study findings demonstrate distinct vector-based transmission dynamics of HPAI H5 at the wild waterfowl-poultry interface. Farm biosecurity strategies must adapt to these recurrent, vector-specific risks.
papers.abstract_zh: 2022年2月起,北美地区出现高致病性禽流感(高致病性禽流感)H5N1的2.3.4.4b分支,凸显了感染风险的动态性、不可预测性和区域性差异。需要开展研究,评估高致病性禽流感H5在野生水禽与商业家禽交界处的时空聚集情况,以更好地理解并缓解这一风险。分析了2022年1月至2026年1月期间,北美地区在野生鸟类和商业家禽中公开的高致病性禽流感H5检测数据,按县进行分析。采用回顾性时空置换模型来识别和扫描检测率高于预期的聚集区域。在野生鸟类中,共报告了17,091例高致病性禽流感H5检测,涉及1,467个县级地点。四种物种,绿头鸭(Anas platyrhynchos)(2,848例,16.66%)、加拿大雁(Branta canadensis)(1,496例,8.75%)、绿翅鸭(Anas carolinensis)(1,364例,7.98%)和雪雁(Anser caerulescens)(1,084例,6.34%),共占检测总数的39.73%。在商业家禽中,分别报告了532例高致病性禽流感H5在火鸡养殖场、148例在蛋鸡养殖场、99例在肉鸡养殖场和89例在商业鸭养殖场。多个跨物种溢出事件呈现出从东向西扩展的趋势。2022年初,绿头鸭的检测先于东北部蛋鸡和鸭子养殖场的暴发事件,而2022年夏季在太平洋和落基山脉西部,加拿大雁的检测与火鸡养殖场的暴发事件重叠。2025年中西部地区出现疫情回升,雪雁和加拿大雁的检测与火鸡和蛋鸡群中的严重暴发事件重叠。此外,在2025年秋季至冬季的上中西部地区,加拿大雁和绿头鸭的检测与商业鸭养殖场的暴发事件重叠。研究结果表明,在野生水禽与家禽交界处,高致病性禽流感H5呈现出基于媒介的特定时空动态。农场生物安全策略必须适应这些反复出现的、基于媒介的特定风险。

papers.title: Limited added benefit of seasonal influenza vaccination before A(H5) vaccination in mice and ferrets challenged with A(H5N1).
papers.abstract: Limited A(H5)-specific vaccine supply is expected early in a potential A(H5N1) pandemic, raising the question of whether licensed seasonal influenza vaccines could enhance protection when administered before A(H5) vaccination. We evaluated this strategy in mouse and ferret models using clade 2.3.4.4b A(H5N1) viruses. Seasonal influenza vaccination induced antibodies to seasonal haemagglutinins but did not induce detectable antibodies against A(H5) and did not consistently enhance A(H5)-directed antibody responses after A(H5) vaccination. In lethal challenge studies, seasonal vaccine priming before A(H5) vaccination was associated with improved outcomes compared with A(H5) vaccination alone in one of three mouse experiments, but this effect was not observed in the other two mouse experiments or in ferrets. These findings suggest that seasonal influenza vaccine priming provides limited added benefit to A(H5) vaccine-mediated protection against A(H5N1) under the conditions tested.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates whether seasonal influenza vaccines could enhance protection against A(H5N1) when administered before A(H5) vaccination in mice and ferret models. The research question arises from the limited availability of A(H5)-specific vaccines during early pandemic phases. The study design involves evaluating the strategy in mouse and ferret models using clade 2.3.4.4b A(H5N1) viruses. Seasonal influenza vaccination was found to induce antibodies to seasonal haemagglutinins but not against A(H5), and did not consistently enhance A(H5)-directed antibody responses after A(H5) vaccination. In lethal challenge studies, seasonal vaccine priming before A(H5) vaccination was associated with improved outcomes in one of three mouse experiments, but not in the other two or in ferrets. The authors interpret these findings as suggesting limited added benefit of seasonal influenza vaccine priming to A(H5) vaccine-mediated protection against A(H5N1) under the tested conditions. The results have specific implications for understanding vaccine strategies in animal models, but the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of generalizability to human populations and limited long-term data.

papers.title: Streamlined CRISPR-based assays for detection and subtyping of H5 and H7 avian influenza
papers.abstract: Avian influenza viruses (AIVs) are zoonotic pathogens that pose an increasing global threat due to their potential for significant economic losses in agriculture, and the risk of a pandemic should human-to-human transmission occur. In light of this, we need rapid, sensitive, and specific tests to detect and differentiate circulating AIVs. Current AIV diagnostic methods require specialized laboratory equipment, limiting their use in the field and in low-resource settings. Here, we develop three CRISPR-based Streamlined Highlighting of Infections to Navigate Epidemics (SHINE) assays that address these limitations. We designed, optimized, and validated a SHINE assay for H5 AIV, achieving 100% specificity when tested on seasonal-influenza-positive clinical samples, and a limit of detection of 121.7 copies/μL. We also developed SHINE assays targeting the 2.3.4.4b A(H5N1) and Eurasian H7 lineages. Together, these SHINE assays offer a promising platform for AIV diagnosis and surveillance, particularly outside laboratory settings.

analysis_en.methods: The methods included designing, optimizing, and validating CRISPR-based SHINE assays for H5 AIV, achieving 100% specificity and a limit of detection of 121.7 copies/μL. Additional SHINE assays were developed for 2.3.4.4b A(H5N1) and Eurasian H7 lineages.
analysis_en.main_results: The SHINE assays for H5 AIV achieved 100% specificity and a limit of detection of 121.7 copies/μL. SHINE assays for 2.3.4.4b A(H5N1) and Eurasian H7 lineages were also developed.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as offering a promising platform for AIV diagnosis and surveillance, particularly outside laboratory settings. The SHINE assays are novel in their ability to address the limitations of current AIV diagnostic methods.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings could inform the development of rapid diagnostic tools for AIVs, particularly in field and low-resource settings, enhancing surveillance and control efforts.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the need for further validation in diverse clinical settings and the potential for sample bias. The evidence strength is moderate due to the preliminary nature of the validation.

papers.title_zh: 基于CRISPR的简化检测和亚型鉴定H5和H7 禽流感方法
papers.source_body_en: Avian influenza viruses (AIVs) are zoonotic pathogens that pose an increasing global threat due to their potential for significant economic losses in agriculture, and the risk of a pandemic should human-to-human transmission occur. In light of this, we need rapid, sensitive, and specific tests to detect and differentiate circulating AIVs. Current AIV diagnostic methods require specialized laboratory equipment, limiting their use in the field and in low-resource settings. Here, we develop three CRISPR-based Streamlined Highlighting of Infections to Navigate Epidemics (SHINE) assays that address these limitations. We designed, optimized, and validated a SHINE assay for H5 AIV, achieving 100% specificity when tested on seasonal-influenza-positive clinical samples, and a limit of detection of 121.7 copies/μL. We also developed SHINE assays targeting the 2.3.4.4b A(H5N1) and Eurasian H7 lineages. Together, these SHINE assays offer a promising platform for AIV diagnosis and surveillance, particularly outside laboratory settings.

papers.title: Genetic Diversity of Clade 2.3.4.4b H5Nx High Pathogenicity Avian Influenza Viruses Detected in Korea During the 2025-2026 Winter Season and Pathogenicity of H5N1 and H5N9 Viruses.
papers.abstract: Clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1, H5N6, and H5N9 high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) were detected in poultry and wild birds during the 2025-2026 winter season in Korea. During this period, 62 H5Nx HPAI outbreaks occurred in poultry, and 63 cases were reported in wild birds. Genome constellation analysis revealed substantial genotype diversity. Most H5N1 and H5N9 genotypes were reassortants containing gene segments derived from East Asian clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 HPAIVs since 2022 and low-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses from wild birds. Notably, the European H5N1 genotype EA-2024-DI.2.1, which spread rapidly across Europe in 2025, and its reassortants were identified in Korea. The novel poultry genotypes were also detected in wild birds, supporting wild bird to poultry spillover, whereas one genotype detected in previous season was identified in small-scale poultry farms. H5N1 (C588) of major 25G2 genotype in poultry and H5N9 (C722) of N9-G2 genotype showed high infectivity in chickens with 103.3 and 103.2 EID50 of median lethal dose (LD50) values, respectively. The predominance of the 25G2 genotype in poultry may have been influenced by efficient infection and virus introduction into high-density poultry production areas, potentially facilitating horizontal transmission under field conditions. In young ducks, H5N1 caused rapid mortality, whereas H5N9 induced limited clinical signs without mortality. Both viruses were transmitted to all contact ducks, increasing the risk of transmission to poultry. Despite intensified surveillance and early detection efforts to limit virus spread, H5Nx HPAIV outbreaks occurred during the 2025-2026 winter season. These findings highlight the need for continued surveillance, together with rapid genomic and pathogenic characterization of newly introduced viruses.

media_mentions.content: Avian Flu Diary Covering Pandemic and Seasonal Flu, Emerging Infectious Diseases, public health, community & Individual preparedness. NOTE: All AFD blogs are written by a human - any mistakes are solely mine. Thursday, September 24, 2026 Virus Research: Genetic Diversity of Clade 2.3.4.4b H5Nx High Pathogenicity Avian Influenza Viruses Detected in Korea During the 2025–2026 Winter Season and Pathogenicity of H5N1 and H5N9 Viruses #19,347 Last December - in addition to reporting numerous biosecurity breaches on farms - South Korea's MAFRA Reported Increased Infectivity & Pathogenicity of This Year's Avian Flu Strains, which - for the first time - included 3 HPAI strains (H5N1, H5N6, and H5N9). Of particular concern, their Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency conducted an evaluation of the infectivity and pathogenicity of one highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (serotype H5N1) and found that the infectivity was more than 10 times higher than in previous years. Details at the time were understandably scant, but today we've a research article which sheds new light on the panoply of viruses behind last year's difficult avian flu season in South Korea. While this is a fairly technical report, and the use of regional nomenclature for H5N1 genotypes further complicates matters, the gist is pretty simple. Last year South Korea was visited by a diverse panoply of H5Nx genotypes (n=16), with at least two - H5N9 N9-G2 and H5N1 25G2 - displaying unusually high infectivity in chickens. H5N1 25G2 was also deadly to ducks, whereas H5N9 N9-G2 spread efficiently in ducks, albeit without producing serious illness. H5N1 25G2 was the source of nearly half (n=30) of last year's 62 South Korean poultry outbreaks, but it was only detected in environmental samples once, making its prevalence in wild birds unknown. Whether 25G2 (or H5N9 N9-G2) will return to South Korea this fall - or turn up in other regions - remains to be seen. Due to its technical nature, I've only provided the link, abstract, and a few excerpts. Follow the link to read the report in its entirety. Genetic Diversity of Clade 2.3.4.4b H5Nx High Pathogenicity Avian Influenza Viruses Detected in Korea During the 2025–2026 Winter Season and Pathogenicity of H5N1 and H5N9 Viruses Yunyueng Jang, Ra Mi Cha, Min-Ji Park, Jong-Min Kim, Eui Hyeon Lim, Gyeong-Beom Heo, Se-Hee An, Bina Lee, Hyun-ji Seo, Kwang-Nyeong Lee, Youn-Jeong Lee, Eun-Kyoung Lee 10.1016/j.virusres.2026.199807 PDF Highlights During 2025-2026, clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1, H5N6, and H5N9 HPAIVs were detected in Korea, causing 62 H5Nx HPAI outbreaks in poultry, and 63 cases in wild birds. Ten genotypes (24G1, 25G2–25G7, and N9-G1–3) identified in poultry, among which 25G2 was the dominant genotype. Most genotypes were reassortants containing gene segments derived from East Asian clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 HPAIVs since 2022 and LPAIVs from wild birds. The 25G2 and N9-G2 genotype showed high infectivity in chickens with 103.3 and 103.2 EID50 of LD50 values, respectively. The 25G2 caused rapid duck mortality, whereas H5N9 caused asymptomatic infection with efficient transmission. ABSTRACT Clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1, H5N6, and H5N9 high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) were detected in poultry and wild birds during the 2025–2026 winter season in Korea. During this period, 62 H5Nx HPAI outbreaks occurred in poultry, and 63 cases were reported in wild birds. Genome constellation analysis revealed substantial genotype diversity. Most H5N1 and H5N9 genotypes were reassortants containing gene segments derived from East Asian clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 HPAIVs since 2022 and low-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses from wild birds. Notably, the European H5N1 genotype EA-2024-DI.2.1, which spread rapidly across Europe in 2025, and its reassortants were identified in Korea. The novel poultry genotypes were also detected in wild birds, supporting wild bird to poultry spillover, whereas one genotype detected in previous season was identified in small-scale poultry farms. H5N1 (C588) of major 25G2 genotype in poultry and H5N9 (C722) of N9-G2 genotype showed high infectivity in chickens with 103.3 and 103.2 EID50 of median lethal dose (LD50) values, respectively. The predominance of the 25G2 genotype in poultry may have been influenced by efficient infection and virus introduction into high-density poultry production areas, potentially facilitating horizontal transmission under field conditions. In young ducks, H5N1 caused rapid mortality, whereas H5N9 induced limited clinical signs without mortality. Both viruses were transmitted to all contact ducks, increasing the risk of transmission to poultry. Despite intensified surveillance and early detection efforts to limit virus spread, H5Nx HPAIV outbreaks occurred during the 2025–2026 winter season. These findings highlight the need for continued surveillance, together with rapid genomic and pathogenic characterization of newly introduced viruses. (SNIP) Genotype 25G2 was the predominant genotype detected in poultry during the 2025–2026 season, accounting for 30 outbreaks. However, it was identified in only one environmental sample collected during an epidemiological investigation of migratory bird habitats. This outbreak pattern differed from those observed during previous seasons in Korea, in which the predominant genotypes were generally similar between wild birds and poultry (Cha et al., 2023; Cha et al., 2025; Cha et al., 2026). The predominance of genotype 25G2 in poultry may have been influenced by higher infectivity under field conditions, particularly in layer farms located in high-density poultry farming areas where HPAI outbreaks were concentrated. However, introduction through environmental contamination associated with wild birds cannot be excluded, and the potential influence of sampling bias resulting from spatial and temporal variations in bird migration and surveillance should also be considered (Hayes et al., 2025; Llanos-Soto, Yaffy, Pavlak and Ivanek, 2025). This study revealed multiple introductions of genetically diverse H5 viruses during the 2025–2026 winter season and demonstrated their relatively high infectivity in chickens. Epidemiological investigations of concurrent outbreaks, together with virus detection and genetic analyses, helped identify potential sources of virus introduction in the affected regions and provided evidence of viral contamination in the surrounding environment. Despite enhanced surveillance and early detection efforts to limit virus spread, H5 HPAI outbreaks still occurred in poultry farms. These findings highlight the importance of continued surveillance in wild birds and poultry, coupled with the rapid genomic and pathogenic characterization of newly emerging viruses, to support the implementation of effective avian influenza control disease. (Continue . . . ) ECDC/EFSA Quarterly Avian Influenza Overview June-August 2026 2025-2026: HPAI's Biggest Surge in Wild Birds to Date (Europe) #19,346 As the above EDC/EFSA chart illustrates, after a couple of lackluster years (2023-2025) avian flu returned to Europe with a vengeance last year. We saw similar upticks in places like South Korea, and North America, but reporting from large swaths of the world - particularly in Asia and Africa - is often lacking (see FAO graphic below). Every 3 months the ECDC/EFSA publishes a highly detailed avian influenza surveillance report, and while they tend to be EU centric, in its 67 pages you'll find ample coverage of outbreaks and infections from around the world on a wide variety of avian subtypes. While today's report covers the slowest part (June-August) of the year, these highly detailed quarterly reports make excellent reference material, and are well worth perusing. This edition does contain one milestone, however; the long-dreaded arrival of HPAI to Australia/New Zealand, which was first reported in June. I've posted the Abstract, and a few excerpts below. I'll have a brief postscript after the break. Abstract Between 5 June and 28 August 2026, 110 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) virus detections were reported in domestic (7) and wild (103) birds in 12 countries in Europe.The number of detections remained at a seasonal low throughout the summer, continuing the decline observed since spring. In contrast to previous years, fewer colony-breeding seabirds were affected, and the geographical range of detections was more limited. Further sporadic detections of HPAI A(H5) virus were reported in wild terrestrial carnivores and pinnipeds. Outside Europe, the epidemic continued in the Americas, where also the HPAI A(H7N3) subtype was detected in Mexico. Following its first introduction to mainland Australia, HPAI A(H5N1) virus spread within local wild bird populations and spilled over to terrestrial carnivores and marine mammals. In the US, the number of dairy cattle farms reportedly affected by HPAI A(H5N1) increased, while detections in captive American minks were reported for the first time. Between 5 June and 31 August 2026, 15 cases of avian influenza virus infection were publicly reported in humans (no fatal cases) in three countries and territories: Bangladesh (one A(H5N1) case), Cambodia (one A(H5N1) case) and China (13 A(H9N2) cases). All human cases reported exposure to poultry or a poultry environment prior to detection or onset of illness. Human infections with avian influenza viruses remain rare and no sustained human-to-human transmission has been documented. The risk posed by avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses currently circulating in Europe remains low for the general public in the European Union/European Economic Area (EU/EEA) and low-to-moderate for those occupationally or otherwise exposed to infected animals or contaminated environments. ©2026 European Food Safety Authority, European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control,European Union Reference Laboratory for Avian Influenza. EFSA Journal published by Wiley-VCH GmbH on behalf of European Food Safety Authority (Continued . . . ) As the chart at the top of this blog indicates, each avian flu season (which runs Oct 1st -Sept 30th) is different, sometimes punctuated by the arrival of new subtypes or genotypes, and often varying in intensity. As we go into a new fall season, migratory birds in the Northern Hemisphere are expected to bring with them a new wave of HPAI from their high-latitude breeding grounds (see H5Nx: Reassort & Repeat). While we can't know what kind of avian flu season lies ahead, now would be a good time to review the things you can do to lower your (currently, low) risk of exposure. WHO Interim Guidance to Reduce the Risk of Infection in People Exposed to Avian Influenza Viruses Backyard Flock Owners: Protect Yourself from Bird Flu (CDC Guidance) UF/IFAS Extension: What Backyard Flock Owners Need to Know about Bird Flu (Influenza H5N1) Wednesday, September 23, 2026 EM&I: Limited added benefit of seasonal influenza vaccination before A(H5) vaccination in mice and ferrets challenged with A(H5N1) Credit ACIP/CDC #19,345 One of the biggest challenges during any future H5Nx pandemic would be the rapid production and timely deployment of a two-dose (given 30 days apart) H5 vaccine to billions of people (see Referral: SCI AM - A Bird Flu Vaccine Might Come Too Late to Save Us from H5N1). While it's not a new idea (see 2008's Seasonal Flu Vaccine May Offer Some Protection To H5N1), the notion of using the existing seasonal flu vaccine as either a `stop-gap measure' - or as a `prime-boost' for the first pandemic jab, during the opening months of an H5 pandemic - has persisted. An early, encouraging 2010 study in the journal Vaccines (Seasonal influenza vaccine elicits heterosubtypic immunity against H5N1 that can be further boosted by H5N1 vaccination) reported: Recent findings indicate that seasonal influenza vaccination or infection of healthy humans may contribute to heterosubtypic immunity against new influenza A subtypes, such as H5N1. Here, we investigated whether seasonal influenza vaccination in a mouse model could induce any immunity against the H5N1 subtype. It could be demonstrated that, largely due to the H1N1 component strain A/NewCaledonia/20/99, parenteral immunization of mice with a trivalent seasonal influenza vaccine elicited heterosubtype H5-reactive antibodies able to confer partial protection against H5N1 influenza virus infection. Furthermore, the trivalent seasonal influenza vaccine was found to be compatible with a whole virus H5N1 vaccine in a heterologous prime-boost immunization regimen, achieving superior efficacy compared to a single immunization with an equivalent low-dose of the H5N1 vaccine. More recent evidence remains both mixed and modest - and has often relied on ferret or mouse models (which may not fully apply to humans) - including: Nature Comms: Adjuvanted Influenza Vaccination Increases Pre-existing H5N1 Cross-reactive Antibodies mBio: Low levels of influenza H5N1 HA and NA antibodies in the human population are boosted by seasonal H1N1 infection but not by H3N2 infection or influenza vaccination EID Journal: Effect of Seasonal Influenza Vaccines on Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Clade 2.3.4.4b Virus Infection in Ferrets EID Journal: Investigation of Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Neutralization by Quadrivalent Seasonal Vaccines, United Kingdom, 2021–2024 Note: Regardless of whether the seasonal flu vaccine directly protects against H5N1 infection, there are still good reasons to get the jab, prior to - and even during - an H5Nx pandemic. It still may provide some small boost to your immune response. Neutralizing antibodies aren't the only immune defense against infection. It could help prevent a co-infection with H5N1 and seasonal flu, which has the potential for being more severe. Co-infections could also help generate a reassorted `hybrid' virus (see Preprint: Intelligent Prediction & Biological Validation of the High Reassortment Potential of Avian H5N1 and Human H3N2 Influenza Viruses). While it may not be the last word on the topic, today we've a study in EM&I from researchers at the CDC's NCIRD Influenza Division, which frankly, offers little encouragement on the effectiveness of using seasonal flu vaccines as a `prime-boost' for H5N1 vaccines. I've only reproduced the abstract and a few excerpts, so follow the link to read the report in its entirety. I'll have a brief postscript after the break. Limited added benefit of seasonal influenza vaccination before A(H5) vaccination in mice and ferrets challenged with A(H5N1) Masato Hatta , Ying Huang , Jeremy A. Duke , Joseph R. Rouse , Chenchen Feng , Xudong Lin , show all Article: 2731495 | Received 29 Jun 2026, Accepted 05 Sep 2026, Published online: 21 Sep 2026 https://doi.org/10.1080/22221751.2026.2731495 Limited A(H5)-specific vaccine supply is expected early in a potential A(H5N1) pandemic, raising the question of whether licensed seasonal influenza vaccines could enhance protection when administered before A(H5) vaccination. These findings suggest that seasonal influenza vaccine priming provides limited added benefit to A(H5) vaccine-mediated protection against A(H5N1) under the conditions tested. However, such studies would likely rely on immunological endpoints rather than direct assessment of protection. Evidence of cross-reactivity alone should therefore be interpreted cautiously when informing decision-making, as it may not reliably predict protection against severe or lethal A(H5N1) infection. In the absence of a clear added benefit, prioritizing seasonal influenza vaccination as a priming strategy to enhance protection against A(H5N1) during the early phase of a pandemic may offer limited value, particularly when resources may need to be directed toward A(H5)-specific vaccination and other countermeasures. Continued efforts to improve the development, availability, and deployment of antigenically similar A(H5) vaccines should remain a priority for pandemic preparedness [13,14]. Today's CDC study reports that prior seasonal vaccination offered little reproducible improvement over H5 vaccination alone (at least, in mice and ferrets). While disappointing, it is hardly unexpected. papers.title: Serological Evidence of Widespread Exposure to H5 Avian Influenza Virus in Arctic Foxes in Svalbard, Norway
papers.abstract: Abstract The continued circulation of H5 clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (HPAIV) has caused extensive mortality in wild bird populations worldwide with increasing spillover to mammals. In 2022, H5 HPAIV emerged in Svalbard, Norway, with subsequent detections in wild birds, walruses, polar bears, and arctic foxes. To understand the population-level exposure among Svalbard arctic foxes, we analysed body fluids from carcasses trapped in 2006-2015 (n = 56), 2023-2024 (n = 112), and 2024-2025 (n = 94) for antibodies to H5 avian influenza (anti- H5), influenza A nucleoprotein (anti-NP), and neuraminidase subtypes using ELISAs, haemagglutination inhibition (HI), and a multiplex assay. Only three samples from 2006-2015 tested positive for anti-H5 and were interpreted as false positives. In 2023-2024, seropositivity for anti-H5 was high (95%), supported by a lower anti-NP seropositivity (85%) and antibody profiles consistent with mixed H5N1 (42%) and H5N5 (52%) exposure. In 2024-2025, anti-H5 and anti-NP seroprevalences remained high (83% and 57%), with H5N5 (87%) exposure predominating over H5N1 (3%). A subset of anti-H5-positive samples tested positive by HI (2023-2024: 30%; 2024-2025: 14%). Juveniles with exposure limited to the previous season had higher odds of anti-H5 seropositivity in 2023-2024 than in 2024-2025 (OR 5.5). Analysis of paired lung extracts from a subset of individuals (n = 63) yielded results concordant with body fluids, using an indirect anti-H5 ELISA adapted for carnivores. Our findings demonstrate widespread H5 virus exposure. Together with occasional reports of progression to fatal HPAI, this highlights the need for continued population monitoring to evaluate ecological consequences.

papers.title_original: Serological Evidence of Widespread Exposure to H5 Avian Influenza Virus in Arctic Foxes in Svalbard, Norway

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the population-level exposure of arctic foxes to H5 avian influenza virus, given the global spread of H5 clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (HPAIV) and its increasing spillover to mammals.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed body fluids from carcasses trapped in three time periods: 2006-2015 (n = 56), 2023-2024 (n = 112), and 2024-2025 (n = 94), focusing on arctic foxes in Svalbard, Norway, where H5 HPAIV emerged in 2022.
analysis.methods: Antibodies to H5 avian influenza (anti-H5), influenza A nucleoprotein (anti-NP), and neuraminidase subtypes were measured using ELISAs, haemagglutination inhibition (HI), and a multiplex assay. Paired lung extracts from a subset of individuals (n = 63) were also analyzed using an indirect anti-H5 ELISA adapted for carnivores.
analysis.main_results: In 2023-2024, 95% of samples tested positive for anti-H5, with 42% showing exposure to H5N1 and 52% to H5N5. In 2024-2025, anti-H5 and anti-NP seroprevalences remained high at 83% and 57%, respectively, with H5N5 exposure predominating (87%) over H5N1 (3%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate widespread H5 virus exposure in arctic foxes, with a shift in dominant subtype from H5N1 to H5N5 over time, indicating potential changes in viral dynamics and host interactions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the importance of monitoring arctic fox populations for H5 avian influenza virus to better understand its ecological impact and potential for spillover to other species, including humans.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited by the potential for false positives in earlier samples and the reliance on serological data without direct viral detection, resulting in moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the population-level exposure of arctic foxes in Svalbard, Norway, to H5 avian influenza virus. It analyzed body fluids from carcasses trapped in 2006-2015, 2023-2024, and 2024-2025 using serological assays. The results showed high seropositivity for anti-H5 in 2023-2024, with a mix of H5N1 and H5N5 exposure, and high anti-H5 and anti-NP seroprevalences in 2024-2025, dominated by H5N5. The findings demonstrate widespread H5 virus exposure in arctic foxes, with a shift in dominant subtype over time. This highlights the need for continued monitoring to evaluate ecological consequences and potential spillover risks. The study's evidence is moderate in strength due to the possibility of false positives and reliance on serological data without direct viral detection.

elements_en.methods: Antibodies to H5 avian influenza (anti-H5), influenza A nucleoprotein (anti-NP), and neuraminidase subtypes were measured using ELISAs, haemagglutination inhibition (HI), and a multiplex assay. papers.title_zh: 北极狐中广泛暴露于H5 禽流感病毒的血清学证据:挪威斯瓦尔巴群岛
papers.source_body_en: Abstract The continued circulation of H5 clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (HPAIV) has caused extensive mortality in wild bird populations worldwide with increasing spillover to mammals. In 2022, H5 HPAIV emerged in Svalbard, Norway, with subsequent detections in wild birds, walruses, polar bears, and arctic foxes. To understand the population-level exposure among Svalbard arctic foxes, we analysed body fluids from carcasses trapped in 2006-2015 (n = 56), 2023-2024 (n = 112), and 2024-2025 (n = 94) for antibodies to H5 avian influenza (anti- H5), influenza A nucleoprotein (anti-NP), and neuraminidase subtypes using ELISAs, haemagglutination inhibition (HI), and a multiplex assay. Only three samples from 2006-2015 tested positive for anti-H5 and were interpreted as false positives. In 2023-2024, seropositivity for anti-H5 was high (95%), supported by a lower anti-NP seropositivity (85%) and antibody profiles consistent with mixed H5N1 (42%) and H5N5 (52%) exposure. In 2024-2025, anti-H5 and anti-NP seroprevalences remained high (83% and 57%), with H5N5 (87%) exposure predominating over H5N1 (3%). A subset of anti-H5-positive samples tested positive by HI (2023-2024: 30%; 2024-2025: 14%). Juveniles with exposure limited to the previous season had higher odds of anti-H5 seropositivity in 2023-2024 than in 2024-2025 (OR 5.5). Analysis of paired lung extracts from a subset of individuals (n = 63) yielded results concordant with body fluids, using an indirect anti-H5 ELISA adapted for carnivores. Our findings demonstrate widespread H5 virus exposure. Together with occasional reports of progression to fatal HPAI, this highlights the need for continued population monitoring to evaluate ecological consequences.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 高致病性禽流感(HPAIV)H5 clade 2.3.4.4b 高致病性禽流感病毒的持续传播在全球范围内导致了死亡率种群的广泛感染,并且对哺乳动物的传播风险正在增加。2022年,H5 HPAIV在挪威斯瓦尔巴群岛首次出现,并随后在野生鸟类、海象、北极熊和北极狐中被检测到。为了了解斯瓦尔巴群岛北极狐种群的暴露情况,我们分析了2006-2015年(n = 56)、2023-2024年(n = 112)和2024-2025年(n = 94)捕获的尸体的体液,检测针对H5 禽流感病毒(anti-H5)、流感A型核蛋白(anti-NP)和神经氨酸酶亚型的抗体,使用ELISA、血凝抑制(HI)试验和多重检测方法。仅2006-2015年的三个样本对anti-H5呈阳性,被解释为假阳性。在2023-2024年,anti-H5的血清阳性率很高(95%),并由较低的anti-NP血清阳性率(85%)和与混合H5N1(42%)和H5N5(52%)暴露一致的抗体谱所支持。在2024-2025年,anti-H5和anti-NP的血清阳性率分别保持在83%和57%,其中H5N5(87%)的暴露显著高于H5N1(3%)。一部分anti-H5阳性样本通过HI试验呈阳性(2023-2024年:30%;2024-2025年:14%)。2023-2024年,仅限于上一季节暴露的幼年个体anti-H5血清阳性率的比值(OR)高于2024-2025年(OR 5.5)。对63名个体的肺部提取物进行配对分析,使用一种针对食肉动物改良的间接anti-H5 ELISA,结果与体液检测结果一致。我们的研究结果表明,北极狐中广泛存在H5病毒暴露。结合偶尔报告的H5 HPAIV进展为致命性病例,这凸显了持续监测北极狐种群以评估其生态影响的必要性。

papers.title: Distinct influenza interfaces in cattle: repeated spillovers of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) from wild birds and enzootic circulation of influenza D virus
papers.abstract: Cattle now occupy two epidemiologically distinct influenza interfaces. This Mini Review comparatively synthesizes epidemiological, pathological, experimental-transmission, genomic, and surveillance evidence for highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) and influenza D virus (IDV), asking how source ecology, tissue tropism, shedding, transmission, persistence, and zoonotic evidence differ between the two viruses. Genetically distinct H5N1 viruses have spilled over repeatedly from wild birds into United States dairy cattle. In lactating cows, infection is prominent in mammary alveolar epithelium and produces high titers of infectious virus in raw milk; inter-herd cattle movements have disseminated genotype B3.13 through dairy production networks. On affected farms, viral RNA has been detected in milk and respiratory specimens; infectious virus is recovered consistently from raw milk and mammary tissues but only sporadically from respiratory or environmental samples such as milking-parlour air and wastewater. These findings identify exposure settings but do not resolve the dominant natural cow-to-cow transmission route or how the virus reaches the mammary gland. Occupational infections have occurred, but sustained cattle adaptation or long-term reservoir status has not been demonstrated. In contrast, IDV is a cattle-adapted respiratory virus maintained through direct contact and short-range airborne transmission, with interlineage reassortment among IDV genome segments and frequent association with bovine respiratory disease complex (BRDC), although an independent causal role in BRDC remains unproven. Human seroreactivity and efficient replication in human airway models indicate exposure and biological compatibility, but not confirmed productive human infection or onward transmission. These contrasts support event-triggered, milk-centered investigation for H5N1 and longitudinal respiratory and genomic surveillance for IDV, built on shared One Health diagnostic, sequencing, epidemiological, and occupational-health infrastructure.

papers.title_zh: 牛中不同的流感界面:A(H5N1)病毒从野生鸟类到野生鸟类的反复跨物种溢出以及流感D病毒的流行性传播
papers.source_body_en: Cattle now occupy two epidemiologically distinct influenza interfaces. This Mini Review comparatively synthesizes epidemiological, pathological, experimental-transmission, genomic, and surveillance evidence for highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) and influenza D virus (IDV), asking how source ecology, tissue tropism, shedding, transmission, persistence, and zoonotic evidence differ between the two viruses. Genetically distinct H5N1 viruses have spilled over repeatedly from wild birds into United States dairy cattle. In lactating cows, infection is prominent in mammary alveolar epithelium and produces high titers of infectious virus in raw milk; inter-herd cattle movements have disseminated genotype B3.13 through dairy production networks. On affected farms, viral RNA has been detected in milk and respiratory specimens; infectious virus is recovered consistently from raw milk and mammary tissues but only sporadically from respiratory or environmental samples such as milking-parlour air and wastewater. These findings identify exposure settings but do not resolve the dominant natural cow-to-cow transmission route or how the virus reaches the mammary gland. Occupational infections have occurred, but sustained cattle adaptation or long-term reservoir status has not been demonstrated. In contrast, IDV is a cattle-adapted respiratory virus maintained through direct contact and short-range airborne transmission, with interlineage reassortment among IDV genome segments and frequent association with bovine respiratory disease complex (BRDC), although an independent causal role in BRDC remains unproven. Human seroreactivity and efficient replication in human airway models indicate exposure and biological compatibility, but not confirmed productive human infection or onward transmission. These contrasts support event-triggered, milk-centered investigation for H5N1 and longitudinal respiratory and genomic surveillance for IDV, built on shared One Health diagnostic, sequencing, epidemiological, and occupational-health infrastructure.
papers.abstract_zh: 牛现在占据了两个流行病学上不同的流感界面。本文简要综述比较了A(H5N1)病毒和流感D病毒(IDV)在流行病学、病理学、实验-传播、基因组和监测方面的证据,探讨这两种病毒在来源生态、组织嗜性、病毒释放、传播、持续性和人兽共患病证据方面的差异。遗传上不同的H5N1病毒已反复从野生鸟类溢出到美国奶牛中。在泌乳牛中,感染主要发生在乳腺泡上皮细胞,并在生乳中产生高滴度的传染性病毒;跨牧场的牛群流动已将基因型B3.13传播至奶业生产网络。在受影响的农场中,病毒RNA在生乳和呼吸道样本中被检测到;传染性病毒可从生乳和乳腺组织中一致回收,但在呼吸道或环境样本(如挤奶厅空气和污水)中仅偶尔检测到。这些发现指出了暴露环境,但并未阐明主要的自然牛间传播途径或病毒如何到达乳腺。职业性感染已发生,但尚未证明牛的持续适应或长期储存宿主状态。相比之下,IDV是一种适应于牛的呼吸道病毒,通过直接接触和短距离空气传播维持其存在,IDV的基因组片段之间存在种间重组,并且常与牛呼吸道疾病综合征(BRDC)相关,尽管其在BRDC中的独立致病作用尚未被证实。人类血清学反应和在人类气道模型中的高效复制表明了暴露和生物学兼容性,但并未确认人类的活跃感染或进一步的传播。这些对比支持针对H5N1的事件驱动、以牛奶为中心的调查,以及针对IDV的纵向呼吸道和基因组监测调查,这些调查建立在共享的One Health诊断、测序、流行病学和职业健康基础设施之上。

papers.title: Interaction between DEAD-box RNA helicase 10 and influenza PB1 polymerase selectively regulates influenza A virus replication.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Identifying the host factors that mediate avian influenza virus adaptation in mammals is important for monitoring zoonotic potential. Although viral polymerase adaptations are known to influence cross-species transmission, the engagement of specific host factors with divergent viral polymerases remains to be explored. We examined human DEAD-box RNA helicases (DDXs) as potential regulators of influenza polymerase activity. A screen of 16 DDXs identified DDX10 as a factor that selectively enhanced the polymerase activity and replication of human-adapted H1N1 viruses, including the 2009 pandemic strain, but not avian-origin H9N2 viruses. This differential activity was associated with DDX10 showing stronger interaction with human-origin PB1 (Cal04/H1N1) than with avian-origin PB1 (BJ16/H9N2). Strain specificity was mediated by two residues (336 and 364) within the PB1 catalytic domain: introducing H1N1-type residues (I336 and I364) into H9N2-PB1 conferred DDX10 responsiveness, while reciprocal mutations in H1N1-PB1 abolished it. This work defines DDX10 as a potential host factor that differentially supports influenza polymerase activity, revealing a specific molecular interface that contributes to the replication efficiency of distinct viral subtypes in human cells and providing insight into host-adaptive mechanisms. IMPORTANCE: This study identifies DDX10 as a strain-specific host factor that differentially regulates influenza A virus replication. By demonstrating that DDX10 selectively enhances human-adapted H1N1 viruses over avian-origin H9N2 viruses through direct interaction with the viral PB1 protein, and by mapping two critical residues (positions 336 and 364) in PB1 that govern this selectivity, our work provides a mechanistic framework for understanding how a single host factor can modulate viral fitness and host adaptation. These findings have important implications for predicting cross-species transmission potential and may guide the development of host-targeted antiviral strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 识别介导禽流感病毒在哺乳动物中适应的宿主因子对于监测人兽共患病潜力至关重要。尽管已知病毒聚合酶的适应性会影响跨物种溢出,但特定宿主因子与不同病毒聚合酶的相互作用仍需进一步探索。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究考察了人类DEAD-box RNA解旋酶(DDXs)作为流感聚合酶活性的潜在调控因子。研究涉及对16种DDXs的筛选,并聚焦于人类适应型H1N1病毒(包括2009年大流行株)和禽源H9N2病毒。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究通过筛选16种DDXs以识别流感聚合酶活性的潜在调控因子。分析了DDX10与病毒PB1蛋白的相互作用,并定位了PB1中的关键残基(位置336和364)。
elements_zh.main_results: DDX10特异性增强了人类适应型H1N1病毒(包括2009年大流行株)的聚合酶活性和复制,但对禽源H9N2病毒则无此作用。这种差异性活性与DDX10与人类来源PB1(Cal04/H1N1)相比,与禽源PB1(BJ16/H9N2)显示出更强的相互作用有关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究将DDX10定义为一种潜在的宿主因子,其特异性调控流感A病毒复制。通过展示DDX10如何通过直接与病毒PB1蛋白相互作用,特异性增强人类适应型H1N1病毒而非禽源H9N2病毒的复制能力,并通过定位PB1中的两个关键残基(位置336和364)来调控这种选择性,我们的研究为理解单一宿主因子如何调节病毒适应性和病毒适应性提供了机制框架。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对于预测跨物种溢出潜力具有重要意义,并可能指导针对宿主的靶向策略的开发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究将DDX10定义为一种潜在的宿主因子,其特异性支持流感聚合酶活性,揭示了特定分子界面,有助于理解不同病毒亚型在人类细胞中复制效率的机制,并提供了关于宿主适应机制的见解。然而,本研究并未探讨这些发现是否适用于其他宿主或病毒亚型。

analysis_en.methods: The study involved screening 16 DDXs to identify potential regulators of influenza polymerase activity. The interaction between DDX10 and the viral PB1 protein was analyzed, and critical residues (positions 336 and 364) in PB1 were mapped.
analysis_en.main_results: DDX10 selectively enhanced the polymerase activity and replication of human-adapted H1N1 viruses, including the 2009 pandemic strain, but not avian-origin H9N2 viruses. This differential activity was associated with DDX10 showing stronger interaction with human-origin PB1 (Cal04/H1N1) than with avian-origin PB1 (BJ16/H9N2).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: This work defines DDX10 as a potential host factor that differentially regulates influenza A virus replication. By demonstrating that DDX10 selectively enhances human-adapted H1N1 viruses over avian-origin H9N2 viruses through direct interaction with the viral PB1 protein, and by mapping two critical residues (positions 336 and 364) in PB1 that govern this selectivity, our work provides a mechanistic framework for understanding how a single host factor can modulate viral fitness and host adaptation.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings have important implications for predicting cross-species transmission potential and may guide the development of host-targeted antiviral strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: This work defines DDX10 as a potential host factor that differentially supports influenza polymerase activity, revealing a specific molecular interface that contributes to the replication efficiency of distinct viral subtypes in human cells and providing insight into host-adaptive mechanisms. However, the study does not address the generalizability of these findings to other host or viral subtypes.

papers.title_zh: DEAD-box RNA解旋酶10与流感病毒PB1聚合酶的相互作用特异性调控流感A病毒复制。
papers.source_body_en: UNLABELLED: Identifying the host factors that mediate avian influenza virus adaptation in mammals is important for monitoring zoonotic potential. Although viral polymerase adaptations are known to influence cross-species transmission, the engagement of specific host factors with divergent viral polymerases remains to be explored. We examined human DEAD-box RNA helicases (DDXs) as potential regulators of influenza polymerase activity. A screen of 16 DDXs identified DDX10 as a factor that selectively enhanced the polymerase activity and replication of human-adapted H1N1 viruses, including the 2009 pandemic strain, but not avian-origin H9N2 viruses. This differential activity was associated with DDX10 showing stronger interaction with human-origin PB1 (Cal04/H1N1) than with avian-origin PB1 (BJ16/H9N2). Strain specificity was mediated by two residues (336 and 364) within the PB1 catalytic domain: introducing H1N1-type residues (I336 and I364) into H9N2-PB1 conferred DDX10 responsiveness, while reciprocal mutations in H1N1-PB1 abolished it. This work defines DDX10 as a potential host factor that differentially supports influenza polymerase activity, revealing a specific molecular interface that contributes to the replication efficiency of distinct viral subtypes in human cells and providing insight into host-adaptive mechanisms. IMPORTANCE: This study identifies DDX10 as a strain-specific host factor that differentially regulates influenza A virus replication. By demonstrating that DDX10 selectively enhances human-adapted H1N1 viruses over avian-origin H9N2 viruses through direct interaction with the viral PB1 protein, and by mapping two critical residues (positions 336 and 364) in PB1 that govern this selectivity, our work provides a mechanistic framework for understanding how a single host factor can modulate viral fitness and host adaptation. These findings have important implications for predicting cross-species transmission potential and may guide the development of host-targeted antiviral strategies.
papers.abstract_zh: 未标注:识别介导禽流感病毒在哺乳动物中适应的宿主因子对于监测人兽共患病潜力至关重要。尽管已知病毒聚合酶的适应性会影响跨物种溢出,但特定宿主因子与不同病毒聚合酶的相互作用仍需进一步探索。本研究考察了人类DEAD-box RNA解旋酶(DDXs)作为流感聚合酶活性的潜在调控因子。对16种DDXs的筛选发现,DDX10能够特异性增强人类适应型H1N1病毒(包括2009年大流行株)的聚合酶活性和复制,但对禽源H9N2病毒则无此作用。这种差异性活性与DDX10与人类来源PB1(Cal04/H1N1)相比,与禽源PB1(BJ16/H9N2)显示出更强的相互作用有关。这种株特异性由PB1催化结构域内的两个残基(336和364)介导:将H1N1型残基(I336和I364)引入H9N2-PB1中可使其对DDX10产生响应,而将H1N1-PB1中的残基替换为H9N2型则会消除这种响应。本研究将DDX10定义为一种潜在的宿主因子,其特异性支持流感聚合酶活性,揭示了特定分子界面,有助于理解不同病毒亚型在人类细胞中复制效率的机制,并提供了关于宿主适应机制的见解。重要性:本研究识别了DDX10作为一种株特异性的宿主因子,其特异性调控流感A病毒复制。通过展示DDX10如何通过直接与病毒PB1蛋白相互作用,特异性增强人类适应型H1N1病毒而非禽源H9N2病毒的复制能力,并通过定位PB1中的两个关键残基(位置336和364)来调控这种选择性,我们的研究为理解单一宿主因子如何调节病毒适应性和病毒适应性提供了机制框架。这些发现对于预测跨物种溢出潜力具有重要意义,并可能指导针对宿主的靶向策略的开发。

papers.title: Evaluating U.S. Federal Zoonotic Records Against National One Health Goals: A Multi-LLM Assessment Across COVID-19, Monkeypox, and H5N1
papers.abstract: (1) Background: Zoonotic diseases require coordinated action across human, animal, and environmental health sectors. While substantial research has focused on outbreak prediction, forecasting, and surveillance, less attention has been given to systematically evaluating how One Health principles are reflected in government policy documents. (2) Methods: We developed a multi-large language model (LLM) framework to evaluate 477 U.S. government documents covering COVID-19, monkeypox, and highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1). Agency technical guidance and Federal Register documents were evaluated using a 19-item rubric covering three goals of the U.S. National One Health Framework: coordination and communication, outbreak response, and surveillance. Claude, GPT, and Gemini independently evaluated the documents. Inter-model agreement and human validation were assessed, and sensitivity analyses examined alternative chunk-to-document aggregation thresholds and the potential influence of document length. (3) Results: One Health alignment was generally limited, with no disease × document-type × goal combination exceeding 39%. Document type showed the clearest differences, with agency technical guidance showing approximately 13–31 percentage-point higher alignment than Federal Register documents across the three goals, while differences across diseases were less consistent. Sensitivity analyses supported the main document-type pattern across alternative aggregation thresholds and after restricting Type B documents by length. After excluding one wording-sensitive rubric item, the three LLMs reached unanimous agreement in 87.1% of document-item evaluations, with human–model agreement (Cohen’s κ = 0.513–0.692) comparable to human–human agreement (κ = 0.649). (4) Conclusions: This study introduces a purpose-built policy corpus and structured multi-LLM evaluation framework for examining how One Health principles are reflected in government documents. The clearest differences were observed across document types rather than diseases, and the main findings were generally stable across alternative analytical assumptions. Together, these findings extend zoonotic-disease research beyond outbreak prediction and surveillance toward systematic evaluation of One Health policy alignment.

Document type showed the clearest differences, with agency technical guidance showing approximately 13–31 percentage-point higher alignment than Federal Register documents across the three goals.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study introduces a purpose-built policy corpus and structured multi-LLM evaluation framework for examining One Health principles in government documents, highlighting the need for more systematic policy alignment assessments.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform the need for improved policy alignment with One Health principles, particularly in zoonotic disease management, and suggest a framework for future evaluations of government records.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the alignment of U.S. federal zoonotic records with the National One Health goals, focusing on highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1) and related zoonotic diseases. Using a multi-LLM framework, the researchers analyzed 477 government documents, finding that One Health principles were generally underrepresented. Document type, rather than disease, showed the most significant differences in alignment, with agency technical guidance scoring higher than Federal Register documents. The study introduces a novel method for assessing policy adherence to One Health principles and highlights the need for more systematic evaluations. However, the findings are limited by potential biases related to document length and wording sensitivity, resulting in moderate confidence in the results.

papers.abstract_zh: (1) 背景:人兽共患病需要在人类、动物和环境健康领域进行协调行动。尽管已有大量研究关注于暴发预测、预测和监测,但对系统评估One Health原则在政府政策文件中的体现却关注较少。(2) 方法:我们开发了一个多大语言模型(LLM)框架,用于评估477份与新冠、猴痘和高致病性禽流感(H5N1)相关的美国政府文件。使用涵盖美国国家One Health框架三个目标的19项评分标准,对机构技术指南和联邦公报文件进行了评估。Claude、GPT和Gemini独立评估了这些文件。评估了模型间的共识度和人工验证,并进行了敏感性分析,以检验不同的文档分块到文档的聚合阈值以及文档长度的潜在影响。(3) 结果:One Health原则的一致性总体有限,没有任何疾病×文档类型×目标组合超过39%。文档类型显示出最明显的一致性差异,机构技术指南在三个目标上的一致性比联邦公报文件高出约13–31个百分点,而不同疾病之间的一致性差异则不太一致。敏感性分析支持了在不同聚合阈值下以及限制类型B文档长度后的主要文档类型模式。在排除了一个对措辞敏感的评分标准项后,三个LLM在87.1%的文档-评分项评估中达成一致,人类与模型之间的共识度(Cohen’s κ = 0.513–0.692)与人类之间的共识度(κ = 0.649)相当。(4) 结论:本研究引入了一个专门构建的政策语料库和结构化的多LLM评估框架,用于探讨One Health原则在政府文件中的体现。最明显差异出现在文档类型而非疾病之间,且主要发现普遍稳定于不同的分析假设下。这些发现将人兽共患病研究从暴发预测和监测扩展到了对One Health政策一致性的系统评估。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明需要改进政策与One Health原则的一致性,特别是在人兽共患病管理方面,并提出了一个用于未来评估政府记录的框架。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究结果受到文档长度和措辞敏感性的潜在影响,但敏感性分析支持了主要的文档类型模式,表明证据强度中等。

papers.title: Estimation of the transmission dynamics of H5N1 HPAI outbreak in a dairy herd using a modeling approach
papers.abstract: The emergence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI 2.3.4.4b) in dairy herds in 2024 across 19 states in the United States of America has raised concerns regarding the potential national and global zoonotic impact. All recent modeling efforts implemented homogenous cattle-to-cattle (both intra and inter-herd) transmission models which did not capture the real-world heterogeneity in mixing of animals, individual variations in susceptibility and infectiousness and clinical incidences across pens and lactation groups. The aim of this study was to develop a heterogenous transmission model to estimate the epidemiological parameters for intra-herd HPAI transmission on Californian dairies. We developed a validated stochastic agent-based model to estimate the epidemiological parameters for intra-herd HPAI transmission on California dairies. The hierarchical agent-based model also parameterized stochastic cattle movements within-herd to simulate real dairy management practices. A cow-level SEIR transmission approach was assumed during the outbreak. A novel Bayesian Optimizer with Gaussian Process (BO-GP) was fitted to the agent-based model for validation which converged within 25-40 iterations (out of 100 per farm) with minimal loss over two distinct error metrics, namely, Poisson loss function and temporal distance metric. Our optimized simulations estimated an average R 0 was around 10.7-10.8 across all farms within the first 15 days of observed outbreak on four dairy farms with a mean effective transmission rate of 4.5% per contact between susceptible and infectious cows within each pen. Our model demonstrated that the movement of cows between pens ensured localized clusters of outbreaks within the sub-herds (pen population) that prolonged the overall outbreak within farms. We estimated the total duration of infection between 14.5 and 28 days, which is higher than the estimates from the homogenous models. With an integrated hierarchical agent-based model combined with Bayesian approximation, we produced actionable insights on the epidemiology of intra-farm spread of HPAI within cow herds, thereby guiding both future model development and applied disease control strategy.

papers.title_zh: 使用建模方法估计H5N1高致病性禽流感在奶牛群中的传播动力学
papers.source_body_en: The emergence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI 2.3.4.4b) in dairy herds in 2024 across 19 states in the United States of America has raised concerns regarding the potential national and global zoonotic impact. All recent modeling efforts implemented homogenous cattle-to-cattle (both intra and inter-herd) transmission models which did not capture the real-world heterogeneity in mixing of animals, individual variations in susceptibility and infectiousness and clinical incidences across pens and lactation groups. The aim of this study was to develop a heterogenous transmission model to estimate the epidemiological parameters for intra-herd HPAI transmission on Californian dairies. We developed a validated stochastic agent-based model to estimate the epidemiological parameters for intra-herd HPAI transmission on California dairies. The hierarchical agent-based model also parameterized stochastic cattle movements within-herd to simulate real dairy management practices. A cow-level SEIR transmission approach was assumed during the outbreak. A novel Bayesian Optimizer with Gaussian Process (BO-GP) was fitted to the agent-based model for validation which converged within 25-40 iterations (out of 100 per farm) with minimal loss over two distinct error metrics, namely, Poisson loss function and temporal distance metric. Our optimized simulations estimated an average R 0 was around 10.7-10.8 across all farms within the first 15 days of observed outbreak on four dairy farms with a mean effective transmission rate of 4.5% per contact between susceptible and infectious cows within each pen. Our model demonstrated that the movement of cows between pens ensured localized clusters of outbreaks within the sub-herds (pen population) that prolonged the overall outbreak within farms. We estimated the total duration of infection between 14.5 and 28 days, which is higher than the estimates from the homogenous models. With an integrated hierarchical agent-based model combined with Bayesian approximation, we produced actionable insights on the epidemiology of intra-farm spread of HPAI within cow herds, thereby guiding both future model development and applied disease control strategy.

papers.title: Risk assessment of avian influenza A(H5N5) virus from the first human case using the ferret model
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The incursion of Eurasian-origin genotype A6 A(H5N5) virus into North America expanded the genetic diversity among North American highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses and heightened concern about zoonotic risk. Following a fatal human infection with the A(H5N5) virus A/Washington/2148/2025, viral replication was assessed in polarized human bronchial epithelial cells, and pathogenicity, transmissibility in direct contact and respiratory droplet models, and airborne virus shedding were evaluated in ferrets to inform pandemic risk assessment. A(H5N5) displayed robust replication in Calu-3 cells at 33°C and 37°C, showing kinetics and peak titers comparable to those of contemporary genotype B3.13 and D1.1 A(H5N1) viruses. In ferrets, A(H5N5) replicated efficiently in the respiratory tract, disseminated to extrapulmonary tissues, and caused fatal disease in all inoculated animals. Airborne transmission was not observed, and infrequent, low-level detection of virus in air samples paralleled that of A(H5) viruses that are not transmissible via air in ferrets. In a direct contact model, limited transmission was detected within 4 days of exposure, with evidence of lower respiratory tract replication in contact animals. These findings indicate that the A(H5N5) virus has the capacity for robust replication in an airway epithelial cell line and can cause severe systemic infection and mortality in ferrets but has not acquired adaptations for airborne spread in mammals. Collectively, these results underscore heterogeneity among clade 2.3.4.4b A(H5Nx) viruses in North America and the need for genotype-by-genotype evaluation of newly emerged viruses to understand public health risk. IMPORTANCE The emergence of Eurasian-origin genotype A6 highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N5) virus in North America has increased viral diversity and raised concerns about zoonotic and pandemic risk. In this study, we evaluated the replication kinetics, pathogenesis, and transmission of A/Washington/2148/2025 A(H5N5) virus, which was isolated from the first reported human infection with this influenza virus subtype, using polarized human bronchial epithelial cells and the ferret model. The A(H5N5) virus replicated efficiently in vitro at temperatures representative of the upper and lower respiratory tracts and caused fatal systemic disease in inoculated ferrets. Limited transmission was observed during 4 days of direct contact. Airborne virus detection was infrequent and did not result in airborne transmission. These findings show that A(H5N5) virus can replicate robustly in mammalian cells and cause severe disease but lacks adaptations supporting efficient airborne spread, informing assessment of the pandemic risk posed by genotype A6 influenza viruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the pandemic risk of the A(H5N5) virus following its emergence in North America, as its genetic diversity and potential zoonotic risk raised concerns about public health implications.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the replication, pathogenesis, and transmission of the A(H5N5) virus in ferrets and polarized human bronchial epithelial cells, using the first human case of A(H5N5) infection as the source of the virus.
analysis.methods: The A(H5N5) virus was tested for replication in human bronchial epithelial cells and for pathogenicity, transmissibility in direct contact and respiratory droplet models, and airborne virus shedding in ferrets.
analysis.main_results: The A(H5N5) virus replicated efficiently in vitro at both upper and lower respiratory tract temperatures and caused fatal systemic disease in all inoculated ferrets. Limited transmission was observed within 4 days of direct contact, and airborne virus detection was infrequent and did not result in airborne transmission.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the A(H5N5) virus has the capacity for robust replication and severe disease in ferrets but has not acquired adaptations for efficient airborne spread, highlighting its potential pandemic risk based on its genetic origin.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform the assessment of pandemic risk posed by genotype A6 influenza viruses and emphasize the importance of evaluating newly emerged avian influenza viruses for their potential to cause severe disease and transmission in mammals.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study highlights the heterogeneity among clade 2.3.4.4b A(H5Nx) viruses in North America and underscores the need for genotype-specific evaluations to accurately assess public health risk, with a moderate confidence in the findings due to the use of a ferret model.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the pandemic risk of the A(H5N5) virus following its emergence in North America, using the first human case as the source. The virus was assessed for replication in human bronchial epithelial cells and pathogenicity in ferrets. Results showed robust replication and fatal disease in ferrets, with limited direct contact transmission and no airborne spread. The findings suggest that while the A(H5N5) virus can cause severe disease in mammals, it lacks adaptations for efficient airborne transmission, which is critical for pandemic potential. The study emphasizes the importance of genotype-specific evaluations for understanding zoonotic risks. However, the use of a ferret model introduces limitations in extrapolating results to human transmission dynamics, reducing the strength of the evidence to moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估A(H5N5)病毒在北美出现后的流行病学风险,因其遗传多样性及潜在的跨物种溢出风险引发了对公共卫生影响的担忧。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究评估了A(H5N5)病毒在雪貂和极化的人类支气管上皮细胞中的复制、发病机制和传播,使用了首例人类A(H5N5)感染病例作为病毒的来源。
elements_zh.methods: A(H5N5)病毒在人类支气管上皮细胞中进行了复制测试,并评估了其致病性、直接接触和呼吸道飞沫模型中的传播能力以及在雪貂中的空气传播病毒脱落情况。
elements_zh.main_results: A(H5N5)病毒在体外于上呼吸道和下呼吸道温度下均能高效复制,并在所有接种的雪貂中引起致命的全身性疾病。直接接触4天内观察到有限的传播,且空气传播病毒检测频率较低,未导致空气传播的传播。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,A(H5N5)病毒在雪貂中具有强大的复制能力和致病性,但尚未获得高效的空气传播适应性,这突显了其基于遗传起源的潜在大流行风险。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果有助于评估A6型流感病毒的疫情风险,并强调了对新出现的禽流感病毒进行评估的重要性,以确定其在哺乳动物中引起严重疾病和传播的潜力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究突出了北美地区2.3.4.4b亚群A(H5Nx)病毒的异质性,并强调了需要进行基因型特异性评估以准确评估公共卫生风险,由于使用了豚鼠模型,研究结果具有中等置信度。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估A(H5N5)病毒在北美出现后的流行病学风险,因其遗传多样性及潜在的跨物种溢出风险引发了对公共卫生影响的担忧。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究评估了A(H5N5)病毒在雪貂和极化的人类支气管上皮细胞中的复制、发病机制和传播,使用了首例人类A(H5N5)感染病例作为病毒的来源。
analysis_zh.methods: A(H5N5)病毒在人类支气管上皮细胞中进行了复制测试,并评估了其致病性、直接接触和呼吸道飞沫模型中的传播能力以及在雪貂中的空气传播病毒脱落情况。
analysis_zh.main_results: A(H5N5)病毒在体外于上呼吸道和下呼吸道温度下均能高效复制,并在所有接种的雪貂中引起致命的全身性疾病。直接接触4天内观察到有限的传播,且空气传播病毒检测频率较低,未导致空气传播的传播。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,A(H5N5)病毒在雪貂中具有强大的复制能力和致病性,但尚未获得高效的空气传播适应性,这突显了其基于遗传起源的潜在大流行风险。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果有助于评估A6型流感病毒的疫情风险,并强调了对新出现的禽流感病毒进行评估的重要性,以确定其在哺乳动物中引起严重疾病和传播的潜力。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究突出了北美地区2.3.4.4b亚群A(H5Nx)病毒的异质性,并强调了需要进行基因型特异性评估以准确评估公共卫生风险,由于使用了豚鼠模型,研究结果具有中等置信度。

papers.title: Acquisition of specific human respiratory tract binding by 2.3.4.4b H5N1 hemagglutinins requires multiple mutations
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT It has been suggested that the hemagglutinin of the human-infecting cattle-derived 2.3.4.4b virus A/Texas/34 H5N1 (H5TX) requires only one mutation, namely Q226L, to switch from binding avian-type to human-type receptor preference. In this study, we examined the binding of H5TX Q226L, along with other key mutations, to sections of human trachea. We conclude that, while H5TX Q226L can bind human-type receptors, more than a single mutation is required for this protein to bind to human respiratory tract tissue. We also report changes in receptor-binding specificity of another 2.3.4.4b HA mutant, H5FR Q226L (from A/duck/France/161108/16 H5N8), associated with the presence of a multibasic cleavage site. This study offers insight into the determinants of evolution toward human-type receptor binding in currently circulating H5Nx viruses. It also emphasizes the importance of testing individual strains using additional methods, including tissue-based approaches, alongside synthetic glycans. IMPORTANCE Currently, H5N1 influenza A viruses are responsible for numerous zoonotic spillover events, from infecting birds to other mammals, including dairy cattle. Although no human-to-human transmission has been observed, several people have been infected. This host range expansion is typically linked to changes in one of the viral surface proteins, hemagglutinin, which can switch its preference from avian-type to human-type receptors. To better understand the potential of the currently circulating H5N1 virus to transmit among humans, we evaluated the effects of the Q226L mutation, in combination with other amino acid substitutions, on binding to the human trachea. We also studied the effect of the multibasic cleavage site, a specific motif present in highly pathogenic influenza strains, on receptor-binding properties. These findings provide insight into the role of receptor binding in influenza infections.

The results indicate that while H5TX Q226L can bind human-type receptors, more than one mutation is required for this protein to bind to human respiratory tract tissue. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过考察突变对受体结合特性的影响,探讨H5N1流感病毒在人类中传播的潜力。已有研究表明,感染人类的牛源性2.3.4.4b病毒A/Texas/34 H5N1(H5TX)的血凝素仅需一个突变,即Q226L,即可从结合禽类受体转变为结合人类受体。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究考察了H5TX Q226L以及其它关键突变对人类气管部分的结合能力。同时研究了多基切割位点,这一在高致病性流感病毒中特有的特定基序,对受体结合特性的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究评估了Q226L 突变与其他氨基酸替换组合对结合人类气管的影响。同时研究了多基切割位点对受体结合特性的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 我们得出结论,尽管H5TX Q226L能够结合人类受体,但该蛋白要结合人类呼吸道组织需要不止一个突变。我们还报告了另一种2.3.4.4b HA突变体H5FR Q226L(来自A/duck/France/161108/16 H5N8)的受体结合特异性变化,该变化与多基切割位点的存在有关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究提供了关于当前流行H5Nx病毒中进化向人类受体结合决定因素的见解。它强调了使用包括基于组织的方法在内的额外方法对单个菌株进行测试的重要性,同时结合合成糖类。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了关于受体结合在流感感染中作用的见解。它们突显了进一步研究的必要性,以理解H5N1病毒在人类中传播的潜力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告具体研究设计的局限性。证据强度中等,因为研究结果基于受体结合实验和基于组织的方法,这些方法可能无法完全反映病毒传播在体内的复杂性。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 有人提出,感染人类的​​牛源 2.3.4.4b 病毒 A/Texas/34 H5N1 (H5TX) 的血凝素仅需要一个 突变,即 Q226L,即可从结合禽类受体偏好转变为结合人型受体偏好。在这项研究中,我们检查了 H5TX Q226L 以及其他关键 突变 与人类气管切片的结合。我们的结论是,虽然 H5TX Q226L 可以结合人型受体,但该蛋白需要多个 突变 才能与人呼吸道组织结合。我们还报告了另一种 2.3.4.4b HA 突变体 H5FR Q226L(来自 A/duck/France/161108/16 H5N8)的受体结合特异性的变化,该变化与多碱基切割位点的存在相关。这项研究深入了解了 进化 在当前流行的 H5Nx 病毒中与人型受体结合的决定因素。它还强调使用其他方法(包括基于组织的方法以及合成聚糖)测试单个菌株的重要性。重要性 目前,H5N1 甲型流感病毒导致许多人畜共患 跨物种溢出 事件,从感染鸟类到其他哺乳动物,包括奶牛。尽管尚未观察到人传人的 传播,但已有多人被感染。这种 宿主 范围的扩展通常与病毒表面蛋白之一血凝素的变化有关,血凝素可以将其偏好从鸟类型受体转变为人类型受体。为了更好地了解当前流行的 H5N1 病毒在人类之间传播的潜力,我们评估了 Q226L 突变 与其他氨基酸取代相结合对与人类气管结合的影响。我们还研究了多碱基切割位点(高致病性流感病毒株中存在的特定基序)对受体结合特性的影响。这些发现提供了对受体结合在流感感染中的作用的深入了解。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过考察突变对受体结合特性的影响,探讨H5N1流感病毒在人类中传播的潜力。已有研究表明,感染人类的牛源性2.3.4.4b病毒A/Texas/34 H5N1(H5TX)的血凝素仅需一个突变,即Q226L,即可从结合禽类受体转变为结合人类受体。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究考察了H5TX Q226L以及其它关键突变对人类气管部分的结合能力。同时研究了多基切割位点,这一在高致病性流感病毒中特有的特定基序,对受体结合特性的影响。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究评估了Q226L 突变与其他氨基酸替换组合对结合人类气管的影响。同时研究了多基切割位点对受体结合特性的影响。
analysis_zh.main_results: 我们得出结论,尽管H5TX Q226L能够结合人类受体,但该蛋白要结合人类呼吸道组织需要不止一个突变。我们还报告了另一种2.3.4.4b HA突变体H5FR Q226L(来自A/duck/France/161108/16 H5N8)的受体结合特异性变化,该变化与多基切割位点的存在有关。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究提供了关于当前流行H5Nx病毒中进化向人类受体结合决定因素的见解。它强调了使用包括基于组织的方法在内的额外方法对单个菌株进行测试的重要性,同时结合合成糖类。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了关于受体结合在流感感染中作用的见解。它们突显了进一步研究的必要性,以理解H5N1病毒在人类中传播的潜力。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告具体研究设计的局限性。证据强度中等,因为研究结果基于受体结合实验和基于组织的方法,这些方法可能无法完全反映病毒传播在体内的复杂性。
