papers.full_text: Disclaimer: Early release articles are not considered as final versions. Any changes will be reflected in the online version in the month the article is officially released. Volume 32, Number 10—October 2026 Dispatch Comparison of Baloxavir-Based Combinations and Monotherapies for Treating Influenza A(H5N1) Clade 2.3.4.4b Virus Infection in Mice Suggested citation for this article Abstract Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b virus continues to cause animal outbreaks and sporadic zoonotic infections. In a mouse model of lethal influenza disease, we compared oseltamivir, baloxavir, and molnupiravir monotherapies with 2-drug combinations. Baloxavir-based combinations improved survival, reduced lung viral loads, and prevented extrapulmonary dissemination, supporting H5N1 preparedness strategies. Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b virus continues to cause widespread outbreaks and sporadic zoonotic infections, underscoring the need to optimize antiviral strategies (1–3). Licensed influenza antiviral drugs can reduce disease severity but might be compromised in severe infections by high viral burdens, treatment delays, and treatment-emergent resistance, motivating evaluation of combination regimens (4–7). Recent H5N1 treatment studies using mouse models suggest antiviral performance can vary by exposure route and disease progression (8–11). To inform preparedness-oriented selection, we compared direct-acting antiviral drugs from distinct classes in a lethal mouse model. We tested monotherapies and 2-drug combinations of 2 licensed influenza antiviral agents, oseltamivir phosphate (OSP; neuraminidase inhibitor) and baloxavir acid (BXA; cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitor), and molnupiravir (MPV; nucleoside analog) to assess whether combinations provided synergistic benefit. We challenged 6- to 8-week-old female BALB/c mice intranasally with A/mink/Spain/3691–8_22VIR10586–10/2022 (5 LD50 [50% median lethal dose]) in a 50-μL inoculum (90 TCID50 [50% tissue culture infectious dose]) (Appendix). We treated mice at 6 hours postinfection (hpi). We administered OSP and MPV orally twice daily for 5 days and administered BXA once subcutaneously. For the low-dose comparison, mice received OSP 25 mg/kg, MPV 25 mg/kg, or BXA 20 mg/kg, and corresponding 2-drug pairs at the same dosages: OSP/MPV, BXA/OSP, BXA/MPV. We monitored body weight and survival through 18 days postinfection (dpi) (n = 7) and quantified infectious virus titers in lung, brain, and heart by TCID50 assay at 4 and 6 dpi (n = 3/time point) (Figure 1; Appendix Tables 1–5). Vehicle-treated mice exhibited rapid weight loss and uniform death. In monotherapy low-dose treatments, OSP or MPV conferred partial protection (2/7 survival each), whereas BXA administered as a single dose was more protective (4/7 survival) and more consistently limited weight loss (Figure 1, panels A–F). Dose-escalation to 50 mg/kg monotherapies also improved outcomes but did not provide 100% protection (Appendix Figures 2, 3), consistent with prior reports showing therapeutic benefit of antiviral drugs in H5N1 mouse infection models (8–11). Accordingly, we evaluated 2-drug regimens in which BXA was maintained at 20 mg/kg and partnered with OSP or MPV at either 25 or 50 mg/kg. Across all three 2-drug regimens—OSP/MPV (25/25 mg/kg and 50/50 mg/kg), BXA/OSP (20/25 mg/kg and 20/50 mg/kg), and BXA/MPV (20/25 mg/kg and 20/50 mg/kg)—combination treatment stabilized body weight and markedly improved survival relative to the corresponding monotherapies (Figure 1, panels A–F; Appendix Figure 3). BXA-containing combinations showed the greatest protection, and no deaths (7/7 survival) occurred through 18 dpi at both dose pairs, whereas OSP/MPV did not show complete protection (Figure 1, panels A–F; Appendix Figure 3). Bliss-independence analysis (12) of end-of-study survival (18 dpi; n = 7/group) showed positive ΔBliss estimates for BXA-containing combinations, most clearly at the 20/25 mg/kg dose pairs. At the 20/50 mg/kg dose pairs, ΔBliss values remained positive but were smaller, consistent with an attenuated interaction at higher antiviral exposure. OSP/MPV showed a weaker, dose-dependent interaction (Appendix Table 6). We observed that clinical benefit paralleled tissue-level virologic control and prevention of extrapulmonary dissemination (Figure 1, panels G–L). At 4 dpi, monotherapy with BXA and OSP, but not MPV, reduced lung titers; brain and heart titers were near or below the limit of detection (LOD), consistent with limited dissemination at that timepoint. By 6 dpi, vehicle-treated mice showed high lung viral loads accompanied by detectable virus in brain and heart. In treated animals, BXA provided the most consistent tissue-level control, keeping viral titers in brain and heart at the LOD; 25 mg/kg OSP or MPV permitted occasional instances of replication in the brain. Combination therapy further inhibited residual dissemination. At 4 dpi, lung titers in combination groups frequently approached the LOD, most prominently for BXA-containing pairs, whereas brain and heart remained at or near the LOD. By 6 dpi, low lung titers were sustained, and systemic spread was largely abolished in BXA-containing groups. In contrast, OSP/MPV combinations showed comparatively weaker lung viral clearance and survival benefit. Nevertheless, those combinations converted partial clinical protection into near-complete or complete survival, reduced pulmonary titers, and prevented neuroinvasion and detectable heart virus that were still observed under some monotherapy conditions. We conducted histopathology and immunohistochemistry and transcriptomic profiling of lung and brain at 6 dpi (n = 3/group) (Figures 2–4). In representative sections, vehicle-treated mice showed prominent influenza nucleoprotein immunoreactivity in both lung and brain (Figure 2), consistent with extensive tissue antigen burden during lethal infection (Figure 1). Across monotherapy groups, nucleoprotein staining and associated tissue involvement appeared reduced but remained detectable. However, combination therapy showed markedly diminished to near-absent nucleoprotein signal in both organs, most consistently the BXA-containing pairs, supporting a tissue-level correlate for the observed improved survival and restricted dissemination. Concordantly, RNA sequencing at 6 dpi demonstrated treatment-associated clustering of transcriptomic profiles by principal component analysis, showing separation between vehicle-treated and antiviral-treated groups. BXA-containing combinations showed tighter clustering than monotherapies in both lung and brain, consistent with a more uniform host transcriptional response under the most protective regimens (Figure 3, panel A; Figure 4, panel A). Pathway analysis identified differential enrichment of host innate immune, inflammatory, and neuronal/synaptic pathways within both tissues. Combination therapies, particularly BXA-containing regimens, showed reduced enrichment of pathways relevant to type II interferon, innate immune response, and inflammatory response compared with monotherapies. Of note, those combinations showed relative preservation of neuronal and synaptic pathways, such as cognition, memory, and vesicle-mediated transport, and profiles shifted closer to uninfected controls (Figure 3, panel B; Figure 4, panel B). Limitations of our investigation included early treatment initiation (6 hpi), modest sample sizes for tissue titration, and the use of MPV, which is not licensed for influenza (13). Exploratory single nucleotide polymorphism analysis of 6-dpi lung viral RNA did not identify canonical PA-I38 or NA-H275Y substitutions in antiviral-treated groups; however, we did not perform targeted deep sequencing and phenotypic susceptibility testing. Because we did not evaluate delayed treatment at 24 or 48 hpi, further studies are needed to determine whether BXA-based combinations retain efficacy when initiated later after infection. Nonetheless, the consistency of BXA-containing combination benefit across dosing regimens (Figure 1; Appendix Figure 3) and across endpoints (clinical course, survival, and tissue infectious virus) supports further evaluation in settings closer to clinical use, including delayed initiation, additional clade 2.3.4.4b isolates, and transmission-relevant models. In a lethal clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 mouse model, monotherapies with OSP, MPV, or BXA improved outcomes in a dose-dependent manner but did not consistently prevent death or extrapulmonary spread. In contrast, 2-drug combinations, particularly those containing BXA, achieved complete survival at both dosing regimens and suppressed pulmonary replication to near LOD while preventing neuroinvasion and cardiac dissemination. Those findings are consistent with recent clade 2.3.4.4b A(H5N1) studies showing strong in vivo activity of BXA and BXA-containing regimens and extend those observations by directly comparing BXA/OSP and BXA/MPV with OSP/MPV in a lethal mouse model (8,10,11,14). Our findings extend recent antiviral-combination studies in less virulent influenza models by showing that BXA-containing combinations provided the strongest protection in a lethal clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 model (14,15). Together, our findings provide an experimentally grounded rationale to prioritize BXA-based 2-drug regimens as a preparedness-oriented option for emergent H5N1 infections when antiviral treatment is initiated early after infection, particularly where severe disease or resistance risk can compromise single-agent performance. The study was conducted in a controlled laboratory setting.
analysis.methods: The study tested monotherapies and 2-drug combinations of oseltamivir phosphate (OSP), baloxavir acid (BXA), and molnupiravir (MPV). Mice were treated at 6 hours postinfection, with OSP and MPV administered orally twice daily for 5 days and BXA given once subcutaneously. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Baloxavir-based combinations showed improved survival and reduced viral dissemination, suggesting their potential value in preparedness strategies for H5N1 infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the use of baloxavir-based regimens in mitigating the severity of H5N1 infections, which could inform future antiviral treatment strategies for avian influenza outbreaks.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the efficacy of baloxavir-based combinations and monotherapies in treating influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b virus infection in mice. The research aimed to address the ongoing threat of highly pathogenic avian influenza, which causes animal outbreaks and sporadic zoonotic infections. Using a lethal mouse model, the study compared the effects of oseltamivir, baloxavir, and molnupiravir monotherapies with combinations. Results showed that baloxavir-based combinations improved survival and reduced viral dissemination, while low-dose monotherapies provided partial protection. The findings suggest that baloxavir-based regimens could be valuable for preparedness strategies against H5N1. However, the study's reliance on a mouse model limits its direct applicability to human infections, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the lack of clinical data.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估基于巴洛沙韦的联合用药和单药治疗对小鼠H5N1亚型2.3.4.4b病毒感染的疗效,因为抗病毒药物(A(H5N1))持续导致动物疾病和零星的人兽共患病。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用了一种致死性流感疾病的小鼠模型,其中6至8周龄的雌性BALB/c小鼠通过鼻腔途径感染了A/mink/Spain/3691–8_22VIR10586–10/2022病毒,剂量为5 LD50,接种体积为50 μL。研究在受控的实验室环境中进行。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在低剂量单药治疗中,OSP和MPV各提供了部分保护,存活率为2/7,而BXA的存活率则更高,为4/7。使用载体处理的小鼠出现了快速体重下降和统一死亡。将剂量提升至50 mg/kg的单药治疗改善了结果,但并未确保100%的保护。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 基于巴洛沙韦的联合用药显示出更高的存活率和更少的病毒扩散,表明其在H5N1感染应对策略中可能具有潜在价值。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持使用基于巴洛沙韦的治疗方案来减轻H5N1感染的严重程度,这可能为未来抗病毒药物应对策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于小鼠模型,因此结果可能无法完全反映人类情况。证据强度中等,因为研究在受控环境中提供了直接观察,但缺乏更广泛的临床验证。

papers.title: Molecular Surveillance and Partial Genetic Characterization of Low-Pathogenic Avian Influenza A Viruses in Migrating Birds from Ukraine
papers.abstract: Wild migratory birds are the principal natural reservoir of influenza A viruses (IAVs) and play a central role in their evolution and global dissemination. Ukraine lies along the Black Sea–Mediterranean Flyway, making surveillance of avian influenza viruses in wild birds essential within a One Health framework, although genomic data from the region remain limited. Between October 2025 and January 2026, 604 cloacal and oropharyngeal swabs and environmental fecal samples were collected from migratory birds and mixed-species flocks in the Tuzlivski lymany National Nature Park and surrounding areas, together with samples from nearby domestic poultry. Influenza A virus was detected by real-time RT-PCR targeting the matrix gene, followed by H5/H7 screening, Oxford Nanopore sequencing of complete hemagglutinin genes, and phylogenetic analysis. Influenza A virus RNA was identified in 30/604 samples (4.97%), whereas all samples were negative for H5 and H7 subtypes. Complete hemagglutinin sequences revealed three low-pathogenic subtypes (H1, H4, and H6) that clustered within established Eurasian lineages closely related to contemporary avian viruses circulating across Europe, Asia, and North America. No influenza A virus or Newcastle disease virus was detected in domestic poultry. These findings provide an important genomic baseline for avian influenza surveillance in Ukraine and demonstrate the value of portable nanopore sequencing and integrated One Health surveillance for monitoring viral diversity and supporting early detection of emerging influenza threats.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 乌克兰位于黑海-地中海迁徙路线,使得在 野生鸟类 中检测 禽流感 病毒的 监测 在 One Health 框架下至关重要,尽管该地区的基因组数据仍然有限。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 完整血凝素序列揭示了三种低致病性亚型(H1、H4 和 H6),这些亚型在已建立的欧亚谱系中聚类,与当前在欧洲、亚洲和北美洲流行的禽流感病毒密切相关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为乌克兰的 禽流感 监测 提供了重要的基因组基线,并展示了便携式纳米孔测序和整合 One Health 监测 在监测病毒多样性和支持新兴流感威胁早期检测中的价值。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告局限性或证据强度。

papers.full_text: Abstract Avian influenza poses a persistent pandemic threat, yet traditional vaccines face production delays. Self-amplifying mRNA (sa-mRNA) technology offers potential advantages, including rapid development, dose sparing, and enhanced, durable immunity. We evaluated ARCT-2304, a bicistronic sa-mRNA vaccine encoding H5N1 hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA), in a Phase 1 randomized, observer-blind trial (NCT06602531). Healthy adults (N = 212) received two doses of ARCT-2304 (1.5, 5, or 12 mcg) or control/placebo on a 4- or 8-week schedule. Primary outcomes evaluated safety and reactogenicity (solicited/unsolicited/serious adverse events [AEs]) and immunogenicity (HA inhibition and NA enzyme-linked lectin assays 28 days post-second dose). Immunogenicity results were benchmarked using serum from a prior study supporting licensure of an H5N1 vaccine. ARCT-2304 was well-tolerated, displaying mostly mild-to-moderate, transient, dose-dependent solicited AEs, with no safety concerns identified. Two doses elicited robust HA and NA humoral responses. An 8-week interval yielded higher magnitude and greater durability than a 4-week schedule, with neutralizing and anti-NA antibodies remaining significantly elevated 6–7 months post-second dose. ARCT-2304 also induced dose-dependent, Th1-polarized T-cell responses peaking at Day 29. These findings support advancing sa-mRNA platforms for pandemic influenza preparedness. analysis.research_question_and_background: Avian influenza poses a persistent pandemic threat, yet traditional vaccines face production delays. Self-amplifying mRNA (sa-mRNA) technology offers potential advantages, including rapid development, dose sparing, and enhanced, durable immunity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Healthy adults (N = 212) received two doses of ARCT-2304 (1.5, 5, or 12 mcg) or control/placebo on a 4- or 8-week schedule. The study was a randomized, observer-blind, dose-finding Phase I trial (NCT06602531).
analysis.methods: Primary outcomes evaluated safety and reactogenicity (solicited/unsolicited/serious adverse events [AEs]) and immunogenicity (HA inhibition and NA enzyme-linked lectin assays 28 days post-second dose). Immunogenicity results were benchmarked using serum from a prior study supporting licensure of an H5N1 vaccine.
analysis.main_results: ARCT-2304 was well-tolerated, displaying mostly mild-to-moderate, transient, dose-dependent solicited AEs, with no safety concerns identified. Two doses elicited robust HA and NA humoral responses. An 8-week interval yielded higher magnitude and greater durability than a 4-week schedule, with neutralizing and anti-NA antibodies remaining significantly elevated 6–7 months post-second dose.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that extended dosing intervals can enhance the durability of sa-mRNA vaccines against H5N1 influenza, offering a promising strategy for pandemic preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support advancing sa-mRNA platforms for pandemic influenza preparedness, particularly in scenarios requiring rapid vaccine development and durable immunity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was a Phase I trial with a limited sample size, focusing on safety and immunogenicity rather than efficacy, which may limit generalizability to broader populations or real-world settings.

analysis.summary_en: This Phase I randomized, observer-blind study evaluated the sa-mRNA vaccine ARCT-2304 against H5N1 influenza, assessing its safety and immunogenicity across different dosing intervals. The study found that an 8-week dosing interval produced higher and more durable immune responses compared to a 4-week schedule. The vaccine was well-tolerated, with mild-to-moderate adverse events. These results suggest that extended dosing intervals could improve the effectiveness of sa-mRNA vaccines for pandemic preparedness. However, the study's limited sample size and focus on immunogenicity rather than efficacy may restrict its applicability to broader populations or real-world settings. The findings highlight the potential of sa-mRNA technology in addressing the challenges of traditional influenza vaccines, particularly in terms of rapid development and durable immunity.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 禽流感构成持续的大流行威胁,但传统疫苗面临生产延迟。自扩增mRNA(sa-mRNA)技术提供了潜在优势,包括快速开发、剂量节省以及增强且持久的免疫性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 健康成年人(N = 212)在4周或8周的间隔下接受两剂ARCT-2304(1.5、5或12 mcg)或对照/安慰剂。该研究是一项随机、观察者盲法、剂量探索的I期试验(NCT06602531)。
elements_zh.methods: 主要结果评估了安全性与反应原性(招募/未招募/严重不良事件[AEs])以及免疫原性(第二剂后28天的HA抑制和NA酶联凝集素试验)。免疫原性结果通过来自先前支持H5N1 疫苗上市许可研究的血清进行基准比较。
elements_zh.main_results: ARCT-2304耐受性良好,主要表现为轻度至中度、短暂且剂量依赖的招募不良事件,未发现安全性问题。两剂诱导了强效的HA和NA体液免疫应答。8周的给药间隔比4周的计划产生了更高的免疫应答幅度和更持久的免疫效果,第二剂后6至7个月,中和抗体和抗NA抗体仍显著升高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究证明,延长给药间隔可以增强sa-mRNA 疫苗对H5N1流感的持久性,为大流行准备提供了一种有前景的策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持推进sa-mRNA平台用于大流行性流感的准备,特别是在需要快速疫苗开发和持久免疫的场景中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是一项I期试验,样本量有限,主要关注安全性和免疫原性,而非有效性,这可能限制其在更广泛人群或真实世界环境中的推广性。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to correct an error in the authorship of the original article on genomic characterization of H6N1 avian influenza viruses from wild birds and domestic ducks in the Republic of Korea and Mongolia (2022–2024).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a correction to the original article, which focused on H6N1 avian influenza viruses collected from wild birds and domestic ducks in the Republic of Korea and Mongolia between 2022 and 2024. The correction addresses an authorship error.
analysis.methods: The correction involved verifying and updating the authorship information of the original article, which was published in Archives of Virology. No new methods or data were introduced in the correction.
analysis.main_results: The correction identified that Kwang-Nyeong Lee should have been denoted as a co-corresponding author in the original article. No new results were presented in the correction.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the correction as a necessary adjustment to accurately reflect the contributions of Kwang-Nyeong Lee. This is a non-novel finding but ensures proper attribution.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The correction has no direct scientific or public health significance beyond ensuring accurate authorship attribution in the published work.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The correction is based on an error in the original article and does not introduce new evidence. The evidence strength is low as it does not provide new findings or data.

analysis.summary_en: This study is a correction to an earlier article on the genomic characterization of H6N1 avian influenza viruses from wild birds and domestic ducks in the Republic of Korea and Mongolia between 2022 and 2024. The correction addresses an authorship error, noting that Kwang-Nyeong Lee should have been denoted as a co-corresponding author. The study does not present new methods, results, or data, but rather corrects an existing error. The correction has no new scientific or public health implications, as it only ensures accurate attribution. The evidence strength is low due to the lack of new findings, and the study does not provide any novel insights into the genomic characteristics or public health relevance of the H6N1 avian influenza viruses.

papers.title: From molecular evolution to the school health room: the role of community-based public health nurses (helsesykepleiere) in one health communication on cross-species influenza transmission in Norway
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have undergone an unprecedented expansion of host range since 2021, moving from wild birds and poultry into dairy cattle, domestic cats, and other mammals, with sporadic human infections in Europe and North America ( Food and Agriculture Organization et al., 2025a ; Rolfes et al., 2025 ). This expansion is underpinned by well-characterised molecular mechanisms of influenza A virus evolution — antigenic drift, gene segment reassortment, and receptor-binding adaptation — that shape the frequency and direction of cross-species spillover ( McDonald et al., 2016 ; Steel and Lowen, 2017 ; Man et al., 2026 ). Norwegian wild-bird and mammalian surveillance data document recurrent incursions of clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, and international risk assessments continue to describe low, but non-zero, human risk concentrated among individuals with close animal contact ( World Health Organization, 2025–2026 ; Ytrehus et al ; European Food Safety Authority et al., 2025a ). Translating this fast-moving virological and epidemiological evidence into everyday protective behavior for children, adolescents, and families remains an underdeveloped link in pandemic preparedness, compounded by documented gaps in adolescent One Health literacy ( Zucca et al., 2021 ). This mini review synthesizes current literature on the molecular basis of influenza cross-species transmission, the Norwegian epidemiological and One Health governance context, and established child- and family-oriented risk-communication frameworks, to argue that Norway’s community-based public health nurses (helsesykepleiere) — who deliver near-universal, statutorily mandated contact with children and families through the helsestasjon- and skolehelsetjeneste — occupy a distinctive but underused position as One Health communication nodes ( Helsedirektoratet, 2021 ). I outline a practical three-tier framework for translating zoonotic-influenza science into age-appropriate household guidance, critically appraise the feasibility, workload, training, and governance implications of this role, and identify priority gaps for future empirical and implementation research.
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解禽流感 A病毒,特别是HPAI A(H5N1) 2.3.4.4b亚型病毒,如何扩展其跨物种传播范围以及对人类健康的影响。它强调了将病毒学和流行病学证据转化为针对儿童和家庭的实用公共卫生沟通策略的空白。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项综述,聚焦于当前关于跨物种传播的分子基础的文献,特别关注挪威的背景。它探讨了社区为基础的公共卫生护士在向儿童、青少年和家庭传递一体化健康沟通中的作用。
elements_zh.methods: 研究方法包括综合现有文献中关于流感A病毒进化的分子机制、挪威监测系统的流行病学数据,以及针对儿童和家庭健康的已建立的风险沟通框架。
elements_zh.main_results: 综述记录了2.3.4.4b亚型禽流感病毒在哺乳动物中的反复跨物种溢出,并强调了与动物密切接触相关的低但非零的人类风险。同时,它也指出了青少年一体化健康素养方面的空白。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,挪威的公共卫生护士在连接病毒学研究与公共卫生实践方面具有独特的优势,提出了一个将人兽共患病流感科学转化为可操作家庭指导的新框架。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,利用公共卫生护士现有的接触网络可以改善社区中人兽共患病的沟通和防控准备,特别是对与动物有密切接触的儿童和家庭。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于现有文献的综述,未提供原创的实证数据,这限制了其结论的强度。然而,它提供了当前知识的全面综合,并指出了未来研究的关键领域。

papers.title: Analytical–Numerical Solution of a Temperature-Dependent Volterra Integro-Differential Model for Avian Influenza Transmission with Saturated Incidence and Environmental Feedback Via an Enhanced Adomian Decomposition Method
papers.abstract: This study presents an analytical–numerical investigation of a temperature-dependent Volterra integro-differential model for the transmission dynamics of avian influenza incorporating saturated incidence and environmental feedback. The model captures both direct transmission among birds and indirect transmission through environmental viral load, while accounting for memory effects via an exponential kernel. The transmission process is modeled using a nonlinear saturated incidence function to reflect realistic contact limitations, and the environmental viral decay is assumed to depend explicitly on temperature. An enhanced Adomian Decomposition Method (EADM) is employed to derive approximate analytical solutions of the nonlinear system. The method effectively handles the coupled integro-differential structure and nonlinear interaction terms. To validate the accuracy and convergence of the analytical solution, numerical simulations are performed using the fourth-order Runge–Kutta (RK4) method. A close agreement between the EADM and RK4 solutions is observed, confirming the reliability and efficiency of the proposed approach. Furthermore, the basic reproduction number (Ro) is derived using the next-generation matrix method, revealing contributions from both direct and environmental transmission pathways. Stability analysis shows that the disease-free equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable when ( Ro 1). The influence of temperature on viral decay is shown to play a significant role in reducing infection persistence, highlighting its importance in disease control strategies. The results demonstrate that incorporating environmental memory, temperature effects, and nonlinear incidence provides a more realistic framework for understanding avian influenza dynamics, and the enhanced Adomian Decomposition Method offers an efficient analytical tool for solving complex epidemiological models.
papers.journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF APPLIED SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICAL THEORY

papers.abstract_zh: 本研究提出了一种温度依赖的Volterra积分微分模型的分析-数值研究,用于分析禽流感的传播动力学,该模型结合了饱和发病率和环境反馈。该模型同时捕捉了鸟类之间的直接传播以及通过环境病毒载量的间接传播,并通过指数核函数考虑了记忆效应。传播过程使用非线性饱和发病率函数进行建模,以反映现实中的接触限制,同时假设环境病毒衰减明确依赖于温度。采用增强型Adomian分解法(EADM)来求解非线性系统的大致解析解。该方法有效处理了耦合积分微分结构和非线性交互项。为了验证解析解的准确性和收敛性,使用四阶龙格-库塔(RK4)方法进行了数值模拟。EADM与RK4解之间表现出高度一致,证实了所提出方法的可靠性和高效性。此外,利用下一代矩阵方法推导了基本再生数(Ro),揭示了直接和环境传播途径对传播的贡献。稳定性分析表明,当Ro < 1时,无病平衡点是局部渐近稳定的。研究还表明,温度对病毒衰减的影响在降低感染持续性方面起着重要作用,突显了其在疾病控制策略中的重要性。结果表明,结合环境记忆、温度效应和非线性发病率能够提供一个更现实的框架来理解禽流感的动力学,而增强型Adomian分解法为求解复杂的流行病学模型提供了一种高效的解析工具。

analysis_zh.main_results: EADM与RK4解之间表现出高度一致,证实了所提出方法的可靠性和高效性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果表明,结合环境记忆、温度效应和非线性发病率能够提供一个更现实的框架来理解禽流感的动力学,而增强型Adomian分解法为求解复杂的流行病学模型提供了一种高效的解析工具。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究还表明,温度对病毒衰减的影响在降低感染持续性方面起着重要作用,突显了其在疾病控制策略中的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告局限性或证据强度。

papers.title: Converging infectious disease threats in the post-COVID era: surveillance fragility, pandemic risk, and global preparedness

papers.full_text: AbstractThe COVID-19 pandemic exposed profound weaknesses in global infectious disease surveillance yet, in its aftermath, pandemic-prone threats have intensified rather than receded. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence on three converging drivers of pandemic risk zoonotic emergence, antimicrobial resistance, and climate-sensitive disease expansion and examines how structural failures in surveillance and global health governance amplify their impact. Drawing on recent epidemiological analyses, policy reports, and One Health evaluations, the review maps post-COVID surges in zoonotic outbreaks, drug-resistant infections, and vector and water-borne diseases, and links these trends to fragmented laboratory networks, inequitable genomic capacity, and weak integration across human, animal, and environmental systems. It further interrogates the geopolitical and socioeconomic determinants of vulnerability, including conflict-related surveillance collapse, vaccine inequity, and the political economy of pandemic financing. Emerging digital tools from AI-enabled forecasting to wastewater and social media surveillance are assessed not only for their technical promise but also for risks related to data bias, extractives, and governance gaps. The review argues that without redistributive investment in One Health integration, regional genomic platforms, community-based surveillance, and enforceable IHR-based accountability, the world will continue to detect converging threats late and respond inequitably, leaving pandemic preparedness structurally fragile in the post-COVID era.Keywords: antimicrobial resistance, climate-sensitive diseases, infectious disease surveillance, one health, pandemic preparedness 2.MethodologyTo construct this integrative narrative review, a targeted literature search was conducted to identify peer-reviewed articles, epidemiological reports, and global health policy documents. The primary search timeframe focused on literature published between January 2020 and June 2026 to capture post-COVID-19 trends; however, foundational studies and critical historical analyses (e.g., pre-pandemic Ebola and Hantavirus outbreaks) published outside this period (2010–2019) were intentionally included to provide necessary epidemiological and ecological context. Databases consulted included PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by grey literature from the institutional repositories of the World Health Organization (WHO), Africa CDC, and the World Bank.The search strategy utilized combinations of the following keywords: (“pandemic preparedness” OR “global health security”) AND (“infectious disease surveillance” OR “One Health” OR “genomic surveillance”) AND (“zoonotic diseases” OR “antimicrobial resistance” OR “climate-sensitive diseases”). Initial identification involved screening article titles and abstracts for relevance, restricted to English-language publications. Articles were then selected for full-text review if they provided empirical data, epidemiological trends, or policy analyses related to post-COVID-19 surveillance infrastructure, digital epidemiology, or the geopolitical determinants of outbreak response. Additionally, a manual backward citation search (snowballing) of the reference lists of included articles was performed to identify further relevant sources that did not appear in the initial database queries.Studies focusing exclusively on the clinical management of specific pathogens without a public health or surveillance context were excluded. The synthesized literature was then thematically organized to analyze three intersecting domains: the biological drivers of outbreak risk, the structural fragmentation of current surveillance systems, and the geopolitical dynamics influencing global health governance. 9.ConclusionThe global infectious disease landscape is becoming more complex, more unpredictable, and more interconnected with each passing year. The failures exposed by COVID-19, Ebola, mpox, H5N1, and cholera have not yet produced a commensurate structural response. The next major outbreak will not announce itself in advance. Whether the global community can detect it early enough, characterize it accurately enough, and respond equitably enough to prevent catastrophe depends entirely on decisions taken in laboratories, legislatures, and multilateral forums before that moment arrives. 1.IntroductionThe COVID-19 pandemic stands as the most consequential infectious disease event of the 21st century. As of March 2024, it had produced approximately 774.8 million confirmed cases and 7 million official deaths globally (1). Three years after peak COVID-19 mortality, the Global Preparedness Monitoring Board of the WHO and World Bank described global pandemic preparedness as remaining “fragile.” Political leaders, distracted by geopolitical frictions and lulled by the easing of COVID-19 death rates, are neglecting the pandemic’s grim lessons, even as new threats loom (2). In 2024, the number of pandemic-prone and epidemic-prone disease outbreaks worldwide was estimated at 301, with approximately 90% associated with COVID-19, dengue, yellow fever, Oropouche virus disease, and influenza (3). A June 2024 analysis by Airfinity and Bloomberg News, drawing on data from over 60 organizations and public health agencies, found that at least 13 infectious diseases are showing a resurgence post-pandemic, with more than 40 countries or territories reporting at least one infectious disease resurgence at 10-fold or more over their pre-pandemic baseline (4).The key drivers of this accelerating burden are well documented. First, falling vaccination rates left populations exposed to vaccine-preventable diseases, with 20 countries in Europe dropping below 90% measles vaccination coverage in 2022 (4). Second, the COVID-19 pandemic caused disruptions to routine immunization programs in at least 68 countries, affecting more than 80 million children worldwide (5). Third, climate change, deforestation, urbanization, and agricultural intensification are expanding the ecosphere in which pathogens can emerge and spread (6). The convergence of these forces ecological disruption, healthcare system strain, post-pandemic fatigue, and structural inequality creates the precise conditions for the next major outbreak (5). A 2024 survey of 103 epidemiologists and virologists by the Abbott Pandemic Defense Coalition found that 75% believe the next major global health challenge will likely occur in the next 5 to 25 years, and that disease surveillance remains the most important tool for identifying the next pandemic. Viral surveillance and wastewater surveillance were identified as the top two investment priorities. These experts also flagged misinformation, distrust in public health officials, and a lack of funding for public health institutions as the primary barriers to sustained readiness (7). Post-COVID reforms including the WHO Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence in Berlin, the Pandemic Fund established jointly with the World Bank, and the Global Health Emergency Corps represent genuine institutional progress. Yet structural inequalities in laboratory infrastructure, genomic surveillance capacity, and One Health integration ensure that the next major pathogen will again be detected late, understood slowly, and responded to inequitably (8). The sections that follow examine the specific threats, the surveillance failures that leave them inadequately detected, and the analytical dimensions of this ongoing global vulnerability.Despite the scale of these threats, few integrative narrative reviews have examined zoonotic emergence, antimicrobial resistance, and climate-driven disease expansion alongside the specific surveillance failures and geopolitical vulnerabilities that collectively shape pandemic risk in the post-COVID era. Existing literature tends to address these domains in isolation, leaving the critical interconnections particularly the compounding mechanisms of threat convergence and the equity dimensions of governance reform underexplored. Therefore, this narrative review aims to explore the intersections of these converging infectious disease threats, analyze the structural failures in global surveillance systems, and highlight strategic priorities for strengthening pandemic preparedness with equity at the center. 3.The evolving landscape of global infectious threats3.1.Emerging and re-emerging zoonotic diseasesZoonotic diseases those transmitted from animals to humans are responsible for an estimated 2.5 billion illnesses and 2.7 million deaths annually, representing nearly 60% of all infectious diseases and 75% of all newly emerging infections (9). The COVID-19 pandemic has set the benchmark for potential future damage, but the biological preconditions for an equally devastating or worse event remain firmly in place (9).H5N1 avian influenza has become one of the most geographically expansive and biologically dynamic threats in the current global health landscape. Since late 2020, clade 2.3.4.4b strains have dominated outbreaks across multiple continents (10). Critically, human cases have continued to occur. In the U.S., an outbreak in dairy cattle first detected in March 2024 resulted in human cases (11). Between September and November 2025, 19 human HPAI infections were reported across four countries, including two deaths (12).The re-emergence of monkeypox (mpox) has been one of the defining infectious disease stories of the 2020s. Following the 2022 global outbreak declared a PHEIC in July 2022 a new and more virulent strain emerged. In August 2024, WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus declared the upsurge of mpox in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and neighboring African countries a second PHEIC, based on the rapid spread of a new clade 1b strain (13). As of September 2024, more than 29,000 cases had been reported with over 800 fatalities, a case fatality rate of approximately 3%. The WHO emphasized the risk of global spread, calling the situation “an emergency not only for Africa, but for the entire globe” (13). Beyond currently circulating threats, novel coronaviruses and other uncharacterized pathogens remain a standing concern. COVID-19 caused a 25% increase in the global prevalence of anxiety and depression in the first year of the pandemic and disrupted education for an entire generation of children in parts of the Global South (5). The WHO has identified over 30 priority pathogens that could cause future global public health emergencies (6).The conditions that produce zoonotic emergence are deepening, not resolving. The wildland-urban interface (WUI) covering just 5% of Earth’s land surface is a prime zone for disease spillover, with nearly 3.5 billion people living at the boundary between cities and wild places (14). A 2025 Yale School of the Environment study mapping wildlife host distribution across the global WUI found that over 700 million people live in areas with suitable habitat for 20 or more zoonotic host species (15). The interplay of human behavior and environmental encroachment is further exemplified by the emergence of Hantavirus and other pathogens linked to expanding ecotourism and travel into previously isolated habitats1. Similarly, recent outbreaks of Ebola virus disease in the DRC underscore how emerging viral threats are fatally compounded by armed conflict and profound community distrust in health systems, allowing localized spillover events to rapidly escalate (doi: 10.1073/pnas.1913980116). In the next 25 years, urban populations will increase by 2.5 billion, with 90% of that growth predicted in Africa and Asia precisely the regions with the highest biodiversity, poorest infrastructure, and greatest undetected pathogen diversity (14). Deforestation, agricultural intensification, informal urbanization, and wildlife trade are together expanding the ecological frontiers at which pathogens move into human populations (9).3.2.Antimicrobial resistance: the silent pandemicAntimicrobial resistance (AMR) is not a future threat, it is a present and escalating crisis. The WHO warns that without urgent action, AMR could cause 10 million deaths annually by 2050, surpassing cancer-related fatalities and threatening to rival the global burden of major non-communicable diseases. Already, AMR directly causes more deaths globally than major communicable diseases like HIV/AIDS and malaria combined (doi: 10.1016/S0140-6736(21)02724-0) (16). In the interim, drug-resistant infections are already complicating routine surgeries, cancer chemotherapy, and organ transplantation (17). Among bacterial pathogens, tuberculosis remains the world’s leading cause of death from an infectious disease, claiming 1.25 million lives in 2023, despite a cure existing for over 70 years (18). The challenge is intensified by the spread of drug resistance. In 2023, an estimated 400,000 people developed MDR-TB or rifampicin-resistant TB globally, and approximately 150,000 died (18). MDR-TB has been reported in virtually every country in the world (16). Extensively drug-resistant TB (XDR-TB) resistant to four commonly used anti-TB drugs has been confirmed in over 127 countries and represents approximately 5% of all MDR-TB cases (19). Only 2 in 5 people in need of DR-TB treatment were diagnosed and started on treatment in 2023 (16). In 2024, only 14% of the estimated 30,000 children with MDR/RR-TB were diagnosed and initiated on treatment (18). The treatment burden is severe: traditional regimens require up to 14,000 pills per patient and can last 2 years (19).Hospital-acquired resistance presents an equally urgent challenge. Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) are designated by WHO as critical-priority pathogens (20). A multi-site study across Ethiopia, Greece, and India found that 22% of 14,078 Enterobacterales isolates were carbapenem-resistant, with Klebsiella pneumoniae resistance rates of 42–54% (21). Alarmingly, resistance is increasingly being reported against WHO “Reserve” group antibiotics such as colistin and cefiderocol which are intended as last-resort options for life-threatening multi-drug resistant infections in healthcare settings (doi: 10.1016/S0140-6736(21)02724-0). In one Saudi Arabian tertiary hospital study of CRE infections, 90-day mortality reached 42.6% (20). Hospital-acquired infections affect between 5 and 15% of hospitalized patients worldwide, with higher prevalence in ICUs and resource-limited settings (22). The ESKAPE pathogens (Enterococcus faecium, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterobacter species) are responsible for the majority of life-threatening hospital-acquired infections and are notable for their capacity to escape the effects of antimicrobial agents (23).Drug resistance is also eroding the treatment of parasitic disease. The cornerstone of malaria treatment globally is artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT). Artemisinin partial resistance, first recognized in Southeast Asia, has now emerged de novo in East Africa in Rwanda, Uganda, South Sudan, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Eritrea, and eastern DRC (24). As of 2024, this represents an ominous shift: ACTs are the most widely used antimalarial drugs in the world, and their failure would dramatically increase malaria deaths (25). In 2024, there were an estimated 282 million malaria cases and 610,000 deaths globally, with 95% of deaths in the WHO African Region, mostly among children under 5 (26). In the United States, dengue cases jumped 359% in 2024 compared to the annual average from 2010 to 2023 (32). The 2024 surge reflects both the growing climate sensitivity of dengue virus transmission and the expanding presence of Aedes mosquitoes…

full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractThe COVID-19 pandemic exposed profound weaknesses in global infectious disease surveillance yet, in its aftermath, pandemic-prone threats have intensified rather than receded. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence on three converging drivers of pandemic risk zoonotic emergence, antimicrobial resistance, and climate-sensitive disease expansion and examines how structural failures in surveillance and global health governance amplify their impact. Drawing on recent epidemiological analyses, policy reports, and One Health evaluations, the review maps post-COVID surges in zoonotic outbreaks, drug-resistant infections, and vector and water-borne diseases, and links these trends to fragmented laboratory networks, inequitable genomic capacity, and weak integration across human, animal, and environmental systems. It further interrogates the geopolitical and socioeconomic determinants of vulnerability, including conflict-related surveillance collapse, vaccine inequity, and the political economy of pandemic financing. Emerging digital tools from AI-enabled forecasting to wastewater and social media surveillance are assessed not only for their technical promise but also for risks related to data bias, extractives, and governance gaps. The review argues that without redistributive investment in One Health integration, regional genomic platforms, community-based surveillance, and enforceable IHR-based accountability, the world will continue to detect converging threats late and respond inequitably, leaving pandemic preparedness structurally fragile in the post-COVID era.Keywords: antimicrobial resistance, climate-sensitive diseases, infectious disease surveillance, one health, pandemic preparedness
full_text_sections.methods: 2.MethodologyTo construct this integrative narrative review, a targeted literature search was conducted to identify peer-reviewed articles, epidemiological reports, and global health policy documents. The primary search timeframe focused on literature published between January 2020 and June 2026 to capture post-COVID-19 trends; however, foundational studies and critical historical analyses (e.g., pre-pandemic Ebola and Hantavirus outbreaks) published outside this period (2010–2019) were intentionally included to provide necessary epidemiological and ecological context. Databases consulted included PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by grey literature from the institutional repositories of the World Health Organization (WHO), Africa CDC, and the World Bank.The search strategy utilized combinations of the following keywords: (“pandemic preparedness” OR “global health security”) AND (“infectious disease surveillance” OR “One Health” OR “genomic surveillance”) AND (“zoonotic diseases” OR “antimicrobial resistance” OR “climate-sensitive diseases”). Initial identification involved screening article titles and abstracts for relevance, restricted to English-language publications. Articles were then selected for full-text review if they provided empirical data, epidemiological trends, or policy analyses related to post-COVID-19 surveillance infrastructure, digital epidemiology, or the geopolitical determinants of outbreak response. Additionally, a manual backward citation search (snowballing) of the reference lists of included articles was performed to identify further relevant sources that did not appear in the initial database queries.Studies focusing exclusively on the clinical management of specific pathogens without a public health or surveillance context were excluded. The synthesized literature was then thematically organized to analyze three intersecting domains: the biological drivers of outbreak risk, the structural fragmentation of current surveillance systems, and the geopolitical dynamics influencing global health governance.
full_text_sections.conclusion: 9.ConclusionThe global infectious disease landscape is becoming more complex, more unpredictable, and more interconnected with each passing year. The failures exposed by COVID-19, Ebola, mpox, H5N1, and cholera have not yet produced a commensurate structural response. The next major outbreak will not announce itself in advance. Whether the global community can detect it early enough, characterize it accurately enough, and respond equitably enough to prevent catastrophe depends entirely on decisions taken in laboratories, legislatures, and multilateral forums before that moment arrives.
full_text_sections.other: 1.IntroductionThe COVID-19 pandemic stands as the most consequential infectious disease event of the 21st century. As of March 2024, it had produced approximately 774.8 million confirmed cases and 7 million official deaths globally (1). Three years after peak COVID-19 mortality, the Global Preparedness Monitoring Board of the WHO and World Bank described global pandemic preparedness as remaining “fragile.” Political leaders, distracted by geopolitical frictions and lulled by the easing of COVID-19 death rates, are neglecting the pandemic’s grim lessons, even as new threats loom (2). In 2024, the number of pandemic-prone and epidemic-prone disease outbreaks worldwide was estimated at 301, with approximately 90% associated with COVID-19, dengue, yellow fever, Oropouche virus disease, and influenza (3). A June 2024 analysis by Airfinity and Bloomberg News, drawing on data from over 60 organizations and public health agencies, found that at least 13 infectious diseases are showing a resurgence post-pandemic, with more than 40 countries or territories reporting at least one infectious disease resurgence at 10-fold or more over their pre-pandemic baseline (4).The key drivers of this accelerating burden are well documented. First, falling vaccination rates left populations exposed to vaccine-preventable diseases, with 20 countries in Europe dropping below 90% measles vaccination coverage in 2022 (4). Second, the COVID-19 pandemic caused disruptions to routine immunization programs in at least 68 countries, affecting more than 80 million children worldwide (5). Third, climate change, deforestation, urbanization, and agricultural intensification are expanding the ecosphere in which pathogens can emerge and spread (6). The convergence of these forces ecological disruption, healthcare system strain, post-pandemic fatigue, and structural inequality creates the precise conditions for the next major outbreak (5). A 2024 survey of 103 epidemiologists and virologists by the Abbott Pandemic Defense Coalition found that 75% believe the next major global health challenge will likely occur in the next 5 to 25 years, and that disease surveillance remains the most important tool for identifying the next pandemic. Viral surveillance and wastewater surveillance were identified as the top two investment priorities. These experts also flagged misinformation, distrust in public health officials, and a lack of funding for public health institutions as the primary barriers to sustained readiness (7). Post-COVID reforms including the WHO Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence in Berlin, the Pandemic Fund established jointly with the World Bank, and the Global Health Emergency Corps represent genuine institutional progress. Yet structural inequalities in laboratory infrastructure, genomic surveillance capacity, and One Health integration ensure that the next major pathogen will again be detected late, understood slowly, and responded to inequitably (8). The sections that follow examine the specific threats, the surveillance failures that leave them inadequately detected, and the analytical dimensions of this ongoing global vulnerability.Despite the scale of these threats, few integrative narrative reviews have examined zoonotic emergence, antimicrobial resistance, and climate-driven disease expansion alongside the specific surveillance failures and geopolitical vulnerabilities that collectively shape pandemic risk in the post-COVID era. Existing literature tends to address these domains in isolation, leaving the critical interconnections particularly the compounding mechanisms of threat convergence and the equity dimensions of governance reform underexplored. Therefore, this narrative review aims to explore the intersections of these converging infectious disease threats, analyze the structural failures in global surveillance systems, and highlight strategic priorities for strengthening pandemic preparedness with equity at the center. 3.The evolving landscape of global infectious threats3.1.Emerging and re-emerging zoonotic diseasesZoonotic diseases those transmitted from animals to humans are responsible for an estimated 2.5 billion illnesses and 2.7 million deaths annually, representing nearly 60% of all infectious diseases and 75% of all newly emerging infections (9). The COVID-19 pandemic has set the benchmark for potential future damage, but the biological preconditions for an equally devastating or worse event remain firmly in place (9).H5N1 avian influenza has become one of the most geographically expansive and biologically dynamic threats in the current global health landscape. Since late 2020, clade 2.3.4.4b strains have dominated outbreaks across multiple continents (10). Critically, human cases have continued to occur. In the U.S., an outbreak in dairy cattle first detected in March 2024 resulted in human cases (11). Between September and November 2025, 19 human HPAI infections were reported across four countries, including two deaths (12).The re-emergence of monkeypox (mpox) has been one of the defining infectious disease stories of the 2020s. Following the 2022 global outbreak declared a PHEIC in July 2022 a new and more virulent strain emerged. In August 2024, WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus declared the upsurge of mpox in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and neighboring African countries a second PHEIC, based on the rapid spread of a new clade 1b strain (13). As of September 2024, more than 29,000 cases had been reported with over 800 fatalities, a case fatality rate of approximately 3%. The WHO emphasized the risk of global spread, calling the situation “an emergency not only for Africa, but for the entire globe” (13). Beyond currently circulating threats, novel coronaviruses and other uncharacterized pathogens remain a standing concern. COVID-19 caused a 25% increase in the global prevalence of anxiety and depression in the first year of the pandemic and disrupted education for an entire generation of children in parts of the Global South (5). The WHO has identified over 30 priority pathogens that could cause future global public health emergencies (6).The conditions that produce zoonotic emergence are deepening, not resolving. The wildland-urban interface (WUI) covering just 5% of Earth’s land surface is a prime zone for disease spillover, with nearly 3.5 billion people living at the boundary between cities and wild places (14). A 2025 Yale School of the Environment study mapping wildlife host distribution across the global WUI found that over 700 million people live in areas with suitable habitat for 20 or more zoonotic host species (15). The interplay of human behavior and environmental encroachment is further exemplified by the emergence of Hantavirus and other pathogens linked to expanding ecotourism and travel into previously isolated habitats1. Similarly, recent outbreaks of Ebola virus disease in the DRC underscore how emerging viral threats are fatally compounded by armed conflict and profound community distrust in health systems, allowing localized spillover events to rapidly escalate (doi: 10.1073/pnas.1913980116). In the next 25 years, urban populations will increase by 2.5 billion, with 90% of that growth predicted in Africa and Asia precisely the regions with the highest biodiversity, poorest infrastructure, and greatest undetected pathogen diversity (14). Deforestation, agricultural intensification, informal urbanization, and wildlife trade are together expanding the ecological frontiers at which pathogens move into human populations (9).3.2.Antimicrobial resistance: the silent pandemicAntimicrobial resistance (AMR) is not a future threat, it is a present and escalating crisis. The WHO warns that without urgent action, AMR could cause 10 million deaths annually by 2050, surpassing cancer-related fatalities and threatening to rival the global burden of major non-communicable diseases. papers.title_original: Converging infectious disease threats in the post-COVID era: surveillance fragility, pandemic risk, and global preparedness

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the growing convergence of infectious disease threats in the post-COVID era, particularly focusing on the fragility of surveillance systems and the risk of future pandemics. The background highlights the increasing prevalence of zoonotic diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and climate-sensitive diseases as critical global health challenges.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted a narrative review of literature published between January 2020 and June 2026, with intentional inclusion of foundational studies from 2010–2019 to provide epidemiological and ecological context. It analyzed global trends in pandemic-prone and epidemic-prone disease outbreaks, including those related to avian influenza.
analysis.methods: The study employed a systematic search strategy across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by grey literature from WHO, Africa CDC, and the World Bank. A manual backward citation search was also performed to identify additional relevant sources, and studies without a public health or surveillance context were excluded.
analysis.main_results: Between September and November 2025, 19 human HPAI infections were reported across four countries, including two deaths. As of September 2024, more than 29,000 cases of MDR-TB or rifampicin-resistant TB had been reported, with over 800 fatalities. In 2024, 14.1 million dengue cases were reported globally, a twofold increase from 2023 and a 12-fold rise compared to 2014.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the re-emergence of monkeypox and the increasing prevalence of MDR-TB and dengue cases underscore the persistent and evolving nature of infectious disease threats. They highlight the need for integrated analysis of these converging risks to inform global preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the urgency of strengthening global surveillance systems and addressing antimicrobial resistance, particularly in regions with high biodiversity and limited infrastructure. They also emphasize the importance of monitoring zoonotic diseases and climate-sensitive pathogens to mitigate future pandemic risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on narrative reviews and the potential for bias in selecting sources. The evidence is moderate, as it synthesizes existing data rather than presenting new empirical findings, and the generalizability of results may be constrained by the focus on specific regions and pathogens.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the converging infectious disease threats in the post-COVID era, emphasizing the fragility of global surveillance systems and the risk of future pandemics. It highlights the increasing prevalence of zoonotic diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and climate-sensitive diseases, such as avian influenza, MDR-TB, and dengue. The authors note that the re-emergence of monkeypox and the rise in dengue cases underscore the ongoing challenges in disease monitoring and response. They stress the importance of integrating surveillance, public health preparedness, and equity in addressing these threats. The study is based on a narrative review of literature from 2010 to 2026, with a focus on avian influenza and related pathogens. While the findings provide valuable insights into current trends, the evidence is moderate due to the reliance on existing data and potential biases in source selection.

papers.title: H1N8 Pathogens
papers.abstract: Genomic Characterization of a Reassortant A/H1N8 Avian Influenza Virus in South American Migratory Shorebirds This Open Science Framework (OSF) project provides the supplementary computational data and analysis outputs associated with the manuscript “Genomic Characterization of a Reassortant A/H1N8 Avian Influenza Virus in South American Migratory Shorebirds.” The study describes the genomic characterization and evolutionary history of a reassortant low-pathogenic avian influenza virus (LPAI) subtype H1N8, isolated from a White-rumped Sandpiper (Calidris fuscicollis) sampled at Parque Nacional da Lagoa do Peixe (PNLP), southern Brazil. The genomic analyses identified a mosaic genome composed of gene segments associated with different South American and North American avian influenza lineages. This OSF repository complements the study's computational repository on GitHub and provides large analysis archives that support the Bayesian phylogenetic, phylodynamic, phylogeographic, host-state and reassortment analyses reported in the manuscript. Repository contents The archived files include: FASTq_222.zip — raw sequencing data associated with isolate PNLP_222. jackknife_history_trees.zip — posterior tree histories generated from the jackknife sensitivity analyses. jackknife_logs.zip — BEAST MCMC log files from the jackknife analyses. NS_NA_logs_trees.zip — Bayesian posterior logs and trees associated with the NS and NA analyses. Relaxed clock.zip — Bayesian analysis outputs generated under the uncorrelated lognormal relaxed molecular-clock framework. Strict clock.zip — Bayesian analysis outputs generated under the strict molecular-clock framework. shared_backbone_logs.zip — Bayesian analysis outputs associated with the shared internal-gene backbone analyses. These files complement the XML configuration files, maximum-likelihood trees, maximum-clade-credibility trees, TreeSort analyses, and Sanger chromatograms available in the associated GitHub repository. The GitHub repository contains the principal analysis inputs and organized supplementary files used throughout the study. Computational reproducibility The complete computational workflow and analysis files are organized in the associated GitHub repository: PNLP_H1N8_Pathogens — GitHub repository The GitHub repository includes the BEAST XML files for relaxed and strict molecular-clock analyses, jackknife analyses, shared-backbone analyses, TreeSort input/output files, ML trees, MCC trees, and Sanger chromatograms. The large BEAST MCMC log and posterior tree archives are additionally deposited in this OSF project to facilitate access to the complete computational outputs of the study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the genomic features and evolutionary history of a reassortant low-pathogenic avian influenza virus (LPAI) subtype H1N8 isolated from a White-rumped Sandpiper in southern Brazil. This research is important due to the increasing concern about avian influenza viruses and their potential to reassort and evolve into more virulent forms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved genomic analyses of an avian influenza virus isolated from a White-rumped Sandpiper sampled at Parque Nacional da Lagoa do Peixe (PNLP), southern Brazil. The research focused on the evolutionary history and reassortment patterns of the virus.
analysis.methods: The methods included genomic characterization using computational tools, with the archived files containing raw sequencing data, posterior tree histories, BEAST MCMC log files, and Bayesian analysis outputs for various frameworks such as relaxed and strict molecular-clock analyses, jackknife analyses, and shared-backbone analyses.
analysis.main_results: The genomic analyses identified a mosaic genome composed of gene segments associated with different South American and North American avian influenza lineages.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the genetic diversity and reassortment potential of avian influenza viruses, which may have implications for their evolution and potential zoonotic transmission.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results contribute to understanding the genetic dynamics of avian influenza viruses, which is crucial for surveillance, diagnosis, and prevention strategies to mitigate the risk of zoonotic transmission and emergence of new viral strains.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to computational and genomic analyses, with no direct clinical or epidemiological outcomes reported. The evidence is moderate as it relies on supplementary data and computational methods without detailed experimental validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study focuses on the genomic characterization of a reassortant low-pathogenic avian influenza virus (LPAI) subtype H1N8 isolated from a White-rumped Sandpiper in southern Brazil. The research aims to understand the evolutionary history and genetic diversity of this virus, which is composed of gene segments from different South American and North American avian influenza lineages. The findings suggest the potential for genetic reassortment and evolution, which could have implications for zoonotic transmission and the emergence of new viral strains. The study is based on computational and genomic analyses, with supplementary data provided in an OSF repository and GitHub. While the evidence is moderate, the results contribute to the understanding of avian influenza dynamics and inform surveillance and prevention strategies.

elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results contribute to understanding the genetic dynamics of avian influenza viruses, which is crucial for surveillance, diagnosis, and prevention strategies to mitigate the risk of zoonotic transmission and emergence of new viral strains.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在描述从巴西南部帕拉库国家公园(PNLP)采集的白腹沙鹬中分离出的重组低致病性禽流感病毒(LPAI)亚型H1N8的基因组特征及其进化历史。由于禽流感病毒的日益关注及其可能重组并进化为更具致病性的形式,这项研究具有重要意义。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及对从巴西南部帕拉库国家公园(PNLP)采集的白腹沙鹬中分离出的禽流感病毒的基因组分析。研究重点在于该病毒的进化历史和重组模式。
elements_zh.methods: 方法包括使用计算工具进行基因组特征分析,存档文件包含原始测序数据、后验树历史记录、BEAST MCMC日志文件以及针对放松和严格分子钟分析、jackknife分析和共享骨架分析等不同框架的贝叶斯分析结果。
elements_zh.main_results: 基因组分析显示该病毒由不同南美和北美禽流感谱系的基因片段组成,呈现出一种镶嵌结构。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果突显了禽流感病毒的遗传多样性和重组潜力,这可能对它们的进化和潜在的人兽共患病传播产生影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果有助于理解禽流感病毒的遗传动态,这对于监测、诊断和预防策略至关重要,以降低人兽共患病溢出和新病毒株出现的风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于计算和基因组分析,未报告直接的临床或流行病学结果。由于其依赖补充数据和计算方法,而缺乏详细的实验验证,证据强度中等。

papers.title_zh: H1N8病原体
papers.source_body_en: Genomic Characterization of a Reassortant A/H1N8 Avian Influenza Virus in South American Migratory Shorebirds This Open Science Framework (OSF) project provides the supplementary computational data and analysis outputs associated with the manuscript “Genomic Characterization of a Reassortant A/H1N8 Avian Influenza Virus in South American Migratory Shorebirds.” The study describes the genomic characterization and evolutionary history of a reassortant low-pathogenic avian influenza virus (LPAI) subtype H1N8, isolated from a White-rumped Sandpiper (Calidris fuscicollis) sampled at Parque Nacional da Lagoa do Peixe (PNLP), southern Brazil. The genomic analyses identified a mosaic genome composed of gene segments associated with different South American and North American avian influenza lineages. This OSF repository complements the study's computational repository on GitHub and provides large analysis archives that support the Bayesian phylogenetic, phylodynamic, phylogeographic, host-state and reassortment analyses reported in the manuscript. Repository contents The archived files include: FASTq_222.zip — raw sequencing data associated with isolate PNLP_222. jackknife_history_trees.zip — posterior tree histories generated from the jackknife sensitivity analyses. jackknife_logs.zip — BEAST MCMC log files from the jackknife analyses. NS_NA_logs_trees.zip — Bayesian posterior logs and trees associated with the NS and NA analyses. Relaxed clock.zip — Bayesian analysis outputs generated under the uncorrelated lognormal relaxed molecular-clock framework. Strict clock.zip — Bayesian analysis outputs generated under the strict molecular-clock framework. shared_backbone_logs.zip — Bayesian analysis outputs associated with the shared internal-gene backbone analyses. These files complement the XML configuration files, maximum-likelihood trees, maximum-clade-credibility trees, TreeSort analyses, and Sanger chromatograms available in the associated GitHub repository. The GitHub repository contains the principal analysis inputs and organized supplementary files used throughout the study. Computational reproducibility The complete computational workflow and analysis files are organized in the associated GitHub repository: PNLP_H1N8_Pathogens — GitHub repository The GitHub repository includes the BEAST XML files for relaxed and strict molecular-clock analyses, jackknife analyses, shared-backbone analyses, TreeSort input/output files, ML trees, MCC trees, and Sanger chromatograms. The large BEAST MCMC log and posterior tree archives are additionally deposited in this OSF project to facilitate access to the complete computational outputs of the study.
papers.abstract_zh: 南美迁徙涉禽中重组A/H1N8 禽流感病毒的基因组特征 本开放科学框架(OSF)项目提供了与论文《南美迁徙涉禽中重组A/H1N8 禽流感病毒的基因组特征》相关的补充计算数据和分析结果。该研究描述了一种从巴西南部帕拉库国家公园(PNLP)采集的白腹沙鹬(Calidris fuscicollis)中分离出的重组低致病性禽流感病毒(LPAI)亚型H1N8的基因组特征及其进化历史。基因组分析显示,该病毒由不同南美和北美禽流感谱系的基因片段组成,呈现出一种镶嵌结构。该OSF仓库补充了研究在GitHub上的计算仓库,并提供了支持论文中报告的贝叶斯系统发育、流行病动力学、流行地理学、宿主状态和重组分析的大规模分析档案。仓库内容 保存的文件包括:FASTq_222.zip — 与分离株PNLP_222相关的原始测序数据。jackknife_history_trees.zip — 来自jackknife敏感性分析的后验树历史记录。jackknife_logs.zip — jackknife分析产生的BEAST MCMC日志文件。NS_NA_logs_trees.zip — 与NS和NA分析相关的贝叶斯后验日志和树。Relaxed clock.zip — 在非相关对数正态放松分子钟框架下生成的贝叶斯分析结果。Strict clock.zip — 在严格分子钟框架下生成的贝叶斯分析结果。shared_backbone_logs.zip — 与共享内部基因骨架分析相关的贝叶斯分析结果。这些文件补充了GitHub仓库中提供的XML配置文件、最大似然树、最大支群可信度树、TreeSort分析和桑格测序图谱。GitHub仓库包含研究过程中使用的主要分析输入和组织好的补充文件。计算可重复性 完整的计算流程和分析文件已组织在关联的GitHub仓库中:PNLP_H1N8_Pathogens — GitHub仓库 该GitHub仓库包括放松和严格分子钟分析的BEAST XML文件、jackknife分析、共享骨架分析、TreeSort输入/输出文件、最大似然树、最大支群可信度树以及桑格测序图谱。此外,大规模的BEAST MCMC日志和后验树档案也存放在该OSF项目中,以方便访问研究的完整计算输出。

papers.title: Epigenetic Regulation of Immune Responses in Chickens: Mechanisms, Host–Pathogen Interactions, and Emerging Genomic Technologies
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation has emerged as a fundamental mechanism governing immune function in poultry by integrating genetic, environmental, nutritional, and microbial signals without altering the DNA sequence. Recent advances in epigenomics have revealed that DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and non-coding RNAs are associated with regulation of immune and inflammatory responses, inflammatory signaling, immune-cell differentiation, and host–pathogen interactions. Poultry-specific studies, predominantly conducted in chickens, have identified infection- and challenge-associated epigenetic changes in models including avian influenza, Marek’s disease, and bacterial inflammatory stimulation, with the strongest current evidence relating to innate and inflammatory immune regulation. Environmental factors such as nutrition, gut microbiota, heat stress, and developmental conditions further shape immune competence through epigenetic programming, while emerging evidence suggests that some epigenetic modifications may contribute to transgenerational disease resistance. Emerging evidence suggests that some epigenetic signatures may persist across generations; however, robust evidence for stable transgenerational inheritance of immune-related epigenetic traits in poultry remains limited. Advances in whole-genome bisulfite sequencing, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, and single-cell multi-omics are improving characterization of the avian epigenome, whereas CRISPR-based epigenome editing, artificial intelligence-assisted prediction, epigenetic selection, and epigenome-informed vaccine optimization remain prospective applications requiring substantial functional and field validation. This review synthesizes current knowledge of epigenetic mechanisms regulating poultry immunity, evaluates their roles in host–pathogen interactions and environmental adaptation, and highlights emerging genomic technologies that may facilitate translation of immunoepigenetic discoveries into practical strategies for improving poultry health, disease resilience, and sustainable production.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the role of epigenetic regulation in immune responses of poultry, particularly in the context of avian influenza, to address the knowledge gap regarding how non-genetic factors influence immune function and host-pathogen interactions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of existing literature focusing on avian influenza in chickens, examining epigenetic changes associated with immune and inflammatory responses, as well as host-pathogen interactions in poultry-specific models.
analysis.methods: The review utilized advances in whole-genome bisulfite sequencing, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, and single-cell multi-omics to characterize the avian epigenome, while prospective applications such as CRISPR-based epigenome editing, artificial intelligence-assisted prediction, epigenetic selection, and epigenome-informed vaccine optimization were discussed.
analysis.main_results: The review found that DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and non-coding RNAs are associated with immune and inflammatory responses, immune-cell differentiation, and host–pathogen interactions in avian influenza models.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as highlighting the importance of epigenetic mechanisms in shaping immune competence and disease resistance in poultry, with the novelty being the integration of emerging genomic technologies into the study of immunoepigenetics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of epigenome-informed strategies for improving poultry health, disease resilience, and sustainable production, with potential implications for understanding and managing avian influenza in both animal and human contexts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on existing literature and the lack of robust evidence for stable transgenerational inheritance of immune-related epigenetic traits in poultry, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of epigenetic regulation in immune responses of poultry, particularly in the context of avian influenza. It highlights how epigenetic mechanisms such as DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNAs influence immune function and host-pathogen interactions. The study evaluates current research on these mechanisms and discusses their potential for improving poultry health and disease resilience through emerging genomic technologies. While the findings suggest the importance of epigenetics in shaping immune competence, the evidence for transgenerational inheritance remains limited. The review also emphasizes the need for further functional and field validation of prospective applications like CRISPR-based editing and vaccine optimization. These insights may inform future research and practical strategies for managing avian influenza in poultry and its zoonotic implications.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨表观遗传调控在家禽免疫应答中的作用,特别是在禽流感背景下,以填补非遗传因素如何影响免疫功能和宿主-病原体相互作用的知识空白。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是对现有文献的综述,重点关注鸡中的禽流感,考察与免疫和炎症反应以及家禽特异性模型中宿主-病原体相互作用相关的表观遗传变化。
elements_zh.methods: 综述利用全基因组基因组亚硫酸氢盐测序、ATAC-seq、ChIP-seq和单细胞多组学技术来表征鸟类表观基因组,同时讨论了基于CRISPR的表观基因组编辑、人工智能辅助预测、表观遗传选择以及表观基因组指导的疫苗优化等未来应用。
elements_zh.main_results: 综述发现,DNA甲基化、组蛋白修饰、染色质重塑和非编码RNA与禽流感模型中的免疫和炎症反应、免疫细胞分化以及宿主-病原体相互作用相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为强调表观遗传机制在塑造家禽免疫能力和疾病抗性中的重要性,其新颖之处在于将新兴基因组技术整合到免疫表观遗传学的研究中。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为制定基于表观基因组的策略以改善家禽健康、疾病抗性和可持续生产提供信息,其潜在影响还可能涉及对动物和人类背景下禽流感的理解和管理。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其依赖现有文献,且缺乏关于家禽中免疫相关表观遗传特征稳定跨代遗传的有力证据,导致其证据评估为中等可信度。

papers.abstract_zh: 表观遗传调控已成为调控家禽免疫功能的基本机制,通过整合遗传、环境、营养和微生物信号,而不改变DNA序列。表观基因组学的最新进展揭示了DNA甲基化、组蛋白修饰、染色质重塑和非编码RNA与免疫和炎症反应、炎症信号传导、免疫细胞分化以及宿主-病原体相互作用的关联。针对家禽的特定研究,主要在鸡中进行,已识别出与感染和挑战相关的表观遗传变化,包括禽流感、马立克氏病和细菌性炎症刺激模型,其中目前最强的证据与先天性和炎症性免疫调控相关。环境因素如营养、肠道微生物群、热应激和发育条件通过表观遗传编程进一步塑造免疫能力,而新兴证据表明,某些表观遗传修饰可能有助于跨代疾病抗性。新兴证据表明,某些表观遗传特征可能在世代间持续存在;然而,关于家禽中免疫相关表观遗传特征稳定跨代遗传的有力证据仍有限。全基因组基因组亚硫酸氢盐测序、ATAC-seq、ChIP-seq和单细胞多组学技术的进步正在改善对鸟类表观基因组的表征,而基于CRISPR的表观基因组编辑、人工智能辅助预测、表观遗传选择以及表观基因组指导的疫苗优化仍属于未来应用,需要大量的功能和现场验证。本综述总结了当前关于调控家禽免疫的表观遗传机制的知识,评估了它们在家禽中宿主-病原体相互作用和环境适应中的作用,并突出了可能促进免疫表观遗传学发现转化为改善家禽健康、疾病抗性和可持续生产的实际策略的新兴基因组技术。

papers.title: One Health
papers.abstract: One Health is an integrative framework that recognizes the functional interdependence of human, animal, plant, and ecosystem health. This chapter examines the concept&s;s historical evolution; its policy landscape at the city, state, national, and international levels; and the ongoing gaps that limit effective implementation. Beginning with foundational definitions and the drivers of One Health relevance, including zoonotic disease emergence, climate change, land-use change, antimicrobial resistance, and biodiversity loss, the chapter surveys U.S. policies across human health, animal health, plant health, and ecosystem protection. Case studies on H5N1 in dairy cattle and poultry and COVID-19 wastewater surveillance illustrate both progress and shortcomings in cross-sector coordination. Occupational health risks at the human–animal interface are also addressed. Key policy gaps identified include siloed data systems, uneven investment in One Health workforce development, lagging environmental surveillance, and disparities between high-income countries and low- and middle-income countries. The chapter concludes by highlighting emerging opportunities, including regional consortia and national academy initiatives, to accelerate intersectoral collaboration and build a more resilient One Health policy framework.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本章对One Health的历史发展进行了全面回顾,分析了其在各级的政策格局以及阻碍其有效实施的差距,重点关注A型病毒及其相关人兽共患病。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为表明需要加强跨部门合作,并识别出关键政策差距,例如数据系统隔离以及高收入国家与低收入和中等收入国家之间投资的差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为制定更加综合的监测和政策框架提供信息,以应对人兽共患病风险并增强公共卫生准备能力。
